      "beyond": "client/frontend/src/videos.css - the phase lists `client/frontend/src/pages/videos/videos.css`, but that file doesn't exist. The home page imports `../../videos.css`, which is `client/frontend/src/videos.css`, so the plan's one `.profile-nsfw` rule went there."

  "replies": {
    "step_1_gather_requirements": "<requirements>\n### Purpose\n\nVideos flagged NSFW are hidden wherever the site lists videos, unless the visitor opts in. Today every video has a nullable `nsfw` INTEGER column in `whitelist.db` (`videos.nsfw`). The crawler fills it, and `/api/video` refreshes it from the source instance (issue 10). The Engine selects the column and passes it through (`engine/server/data/random_videos.py`, `metadata.py`, `search.py`), but nothing filters on it, and `client/frontend` has no NSFW control. After this build a visitor who does nothing never sees an NSFW-flagged video in any list.\n\n### The setting\n\n- A single NSFW setting. Its only control is in the Profile modal (`#profile-section`, rendered by `renderProfileSection` in `client/frontend/src/pages/videos/index.ts`).\n- The control appears in every state the modal renders: a keyless visitor, a visitor holding a key, and the just-issued-key view. It needs no profile key.\n- Default: filter on (NSFW hidden). Turning it off shows NSFW videos.\n- The setting applies everywhere listed under \"Coverage\". There is no other control.\n- Changing the setting on the home page reloads the current feed, so the change shows immediately.\n\n### No per-mode toggles\n\nThe request's toggle buttons on the Recommendations and Random feed modes are dropped at the operator's decision. The feed-mode switcher (`[data-feed-mode]` buttons) is unchanged.\n\n### Storage\n\n- The setting is stored in the browser's `localStorage` only, next to `feedParams:v1` (`client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts`). It persists across reloads.\n- It is not stored server-side and does not follow a profile key to another browser.\n- Missing, unreadable (quota or private mode) or corrupt storage means filter on. A storage write failure must not break the page; the choice still holds for the current page.\n\n### Coverage\n\nThe filter applies to every video list the site requests from the Engine:\n- All five home feed modes: Recommendations, Hot, Recent, Random and Popular (`/recommendations` with `mode=`).\n- The up-next feed: `/videos/similar` and `/recommendations` with a seed `id`, as requested by the video page (`client/frontend/src/pages/video-page/index.ts`) and by the home page with `?id=`.\n- Search (`/api/v1/search/videos`, `client/frontend/src/pages/search/index.ts`).\n\nThe channels page (`client/frontend/src/pages/channels`) lists channels only and fetches no video rows, so it is unaffected.\n\n### Filtering happens in the Engine\n\n- The Engine leaves NSFW rows out while it builds each pool or page, so a page is still filled to its requested size. This covers the home like-layer and mixer layer pools (layer slots filled by ratio), the up-next pool (about 17 rows deep, then the weighted draw), the ordered Hot/Recent/Popular pages (LIMIT/OFFSET paging must not skip or repeat rows under the filter), the random draw, and search results.\n- The browser never drops rows from a page after it arrives, and the gateway (`client/backend/server.py`) does not filter NSFW rows out of the payload either.\n- With the filter off, results are identical to today's.\n\n### Request parameter\n\n- One query parameter, `nsfw`. `nsfw=1` means include NSFW rows. A missing parameter, an empty value, or any other value means filtered. A request that omits it never receives an NSFW-flagged row.\n- The frontend sends `nsfw=1` only when the visitor has turned the filter off, on every feed, up-next and search request.\n- The gateway allowlist `PROXY_ALLOWED_QUERY_PARAMS` in `client/backend/server.py` gains `nsfw` for `/recommendations`, `/videos/similar` and `/api/v1/search/videos`, and the gateway forwards it to the Engine.\n\n### Unknown flags\n\n`nsfw` NULL counts as not NSFW: with the filter on, only rows with `nsfw = 1` are removed (`v.nsfw IS NULL OR v.nsfw = 0` passes). The operator chose this without a measurement, and no `whitelist.db` is in the tree to measure against.\n\n### Random feed page size\n\n`random-cache.db` is prebuilt and holds rowids (`data/random_cache.fetch_random_rowids`, then `data/metadata.fetch_metadata`). With the filter on, the Random feed must still return a full page. The design chooses and justifies one of two approaches: read each drawn video's flag at draw time and draw again or overdraw to refill, or store the flag in the cache. If the cache schema changes, the rebuild and upgrade path must be stated.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- A warning or overlay on a video page opened directly (for example from a link) for an NSFW video. The video page plays whatever it is linked to.\n- Server-side storage of the setting on the profile key (`user_db`).\n- Toggle buttons on individual feed modes.\n\n### Baseline suite state\n\nThe pre-build suite exited 0 (baseline variant: false). The run selected `test_search_fusion.py` (10 passed); the other 29 test groups were unchanged. The build must leave the suite green.\n</requirements>\n\n<conflicts>\nRequest \"Recommendations and Random feed modes each get a toggle button for the NSFW filter\" vs operator decision (Q1): the mode toggles are dropped and the Profile setting is the only control.\nRequest \"Home: a setting in the Profile modal turns the filter off\" (home only) vs operator decision (Q2): the Profile setting applies everywhere, meaning all five home modes, up-next and search.\nRequest \"Random cache: check which keeps the random draw's page size\" vs tree: `fetch_random_rows_from_cache` in `engine/server/data/random_videos.py` already returns fewer than `limit` rows when `fetch_metadata` drops a rowid (for example past `error_threshold`), so today's random page is not guaranteed full even without the filter. The full-page requirement makes the design fix the refill for both causes, or name error-threshold shrinkage as an existing, accepted exception.\nRequest Q3 option \"keyless visitors must get the filtered default\" plus operator choice of localStorage-only vs the gateway: `client/backend/server.py` `_profile_filter` applies keyed profile state server-side, but the NSFW setting never reaches the gateway except as the forwarded `nsfw` query parameter. A keyed profile's setting therefore does not carry to a second browser. This is accepted per the operator's choice and is not a defect.\n</conflicts>",
    "step_2_develop_solution": "<initial_solution>\n### Approach\n\nOne request flag, `include_nsfw`, is parsed once at the Engine's edge. It travels explicitly wherever the call chain is short. Where the call chain runs through the recommendation strategy's generator protocol, it goes through the request context that already carries excluded keys, likes and dislike centroids. Filtering is a SQL predicate, `(v.nsfw IS NULL OR v.nsfw = 0)`, added to the queries that build each pool, so LIMITs count only rows that are allowed. Nothing drops rows after a page is assembled.\n\n**Engine edge (`engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py`).** A parser treats only the exact value `1` as include. It deliberately does not use `_parse_bool`, which also accepts `true`, `yes` and `on`; the requirement says any other value means filtered. `_handle_similar` covers the POST `/recommendations` and `/videos/similar` routes and the GET `/videos/{id}/similar` alias. It parses `nsfw` from the query and stores it in the request context through a new setter and getter pair in `request_context.py`. The getter returns \"filtered\" when the value is unset, and `clear_request_context` clears it. `_handle_search` parses it the same way and passes it to `search_videos`. A request without the parameter is filtered on every route.\n\n**Data layer: an explicit keyword whose default keeps today's behaviour.** `fetch_metadata`, `fetch_metadata_by_ids` / `_select_metadata`, `fetch_random_rows`, `fetch_recent_videos`, `fetch_popular_videos`, `fetch_ordered_page`, `fetch_random_rows_from_cache`, `lexical_candidates`, `vector_candidates` and `search_videos` each gain `include_nsfw: bool = True`. When it is False they add the predicate next to the existing `error_threshold` clause, which already uses the same WHERE/AND pattern. The default stays include because these helpers also serve non-listing callers that must not change: `/api/video` (the video page plays whatever it is linked to), `/internal/videos/*` (resolving likes and blocks), and the ANN compute that writes the similarity cache. \"Filtered by default\" is enforced at the request edge, not in the data layer.\n\n**How each coverage item is met:**\n- **Hot, Recent and Popular (ordered pages).** `_handle_ordered_feed` passes the flag to `fetch_ordered_page`, so the predicate sits inside the ordered query. OFFSET then counts over the filtered total order, and each chunk continues exactly where the last ended. Rows are neither skipped nor repeated, and NSFW rows no longer use up the `ORDERED_FEED_MAX_CHUNKS` budget.\n- **Random feed, the home fallback and the random seed path.** `_fetch_random_rows` passes the flag to both the cache draw and the `ORDER BY RANDOM()` fallback. The cache refill is described under \"Random feed page size\" below.\n- **Recommendations (mixer).** `RecommendationBuilderDeps` gains `fetch_include_nsfw`. It defaults to a callable that returns False, so the keyword construction in `tests/active/test_video.py` still builds, and `server.py` wires in the request-context getter. The builder's existing `*_filtered` closures pass the flag into the random, cache, recent and popular fetches, so those layers are filled at the SQL level. The builder also wraps `get_similar_candidates` so the like-layer sources run with a policy carrying the flag. `SimilarityCandidatesPolicy` gains `include_nsfw`, and the sources stay unchanged.\n- **Like layer and up-next pools.** `_build_rows` in `data/similarity_candidates.py` passes the flag to `fetch_metadata_by_ids`. NSFW entries find no metadata and are skipped before the author cap and before the count toward `limit`. `UpnextPoolPolicy` gains `include_nsfw`, set by `_handle_seed_with_embedding`. `_upnext_rows` counts the filtered pool, so the existing floored ANN fallback widens nprobe and search_limit until `target_min_pool` (about 17) is reached, and only then does the weighted draw run. The refill this needs is the mechanism that already exists. `_handle_vector_search` passes the flag too.\n- **Search.** `lexical_candidates` puts the predicate in the FTS query, so its `candidate_pool` LIMIT counts only allowed rows. `vector_candidates` passes the flag to `fetch_metadata`. The fused list, its `total` and page slicing are all computed after filtering, so pages stay consistent.\n- **Filter off.** Every change is an added clause or an extra draw that runs only when the flag is False. With `nsfw=1` the SQL, the draws and the pools are byte-for-byte today's.\n\n**Random feed page size: read the flag at draw time and redraw.** When the filter is on, `fetch_random_rows_from_cache` draws its usual contiguous window, resolves it with `fetch_metadata(include_nsfw=False)`, and draws further random windows while the page is short. It skips rowids already seen and appends in draw order until the page reaches `limit`. The number of draws is capped by a named constant (4, matching `ORDERED_FEED_MAX_CHUNKS`). With the filter off it makes exactly one draw, as today. That matters: always refilling would also start refilling pages that `error_threshold` drops short, which would change filter-off results. The cache schema does not change, so no rebuild or upgrade is needed.\n\n**Gateway (`client/backend/server.py`).** `nsfw` is added to the `PROXY_ALLOWED_QUERY_PARAMS` sets for `/recommendations`, `/videos/similar` and `/api/v1/search/videos`. The existing sanitiser already forwards allowed parameters and drops empty values; an empty value correctly becomes \"missing\" and so \"filtered\". The gateway's row filter (blocks and dislikes) is not touched, and it does not look at `nsfw`.\n\n**Frontend.**\n- **Storage (`client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts`).** The setting lives here under its own key, `nsfwFilter:v1`. The module gains read, set and query-entry helpers. Only a stored value that explicitly means \"off\" turns the filter off; a missing, unreadable or corrupt value reads as on. A module-level in-memory value holds the choice when `setItem` throws, so it still applies on the current page. This is the same try/ignore pattern `persistFeedParams` uses.\n- **Requests.** `buildSimilarUrl` in `data/videos.ts` appends `nsfw=1` when the filter is off. That one change covers the home feed modes, the home `?id=` up-next feed and the video page's up-next feed, since all three go through it. `fetchSearchResults` in `data/search.ts` does the same, and the comment there that names exactly four parameters gets updated. The keyless search cache is keyed by URL, so on and off results never share a cache entry.\n- **Control (`renderProfileSection` in `pages/videos/index.ts`).** A small helper builds a \"Hide NSFW videos\" checkbox, checked by default. It is appended in all three branches: the issued-key view, the key-holding view and the keyless view. Its change handler saves the setting, then calls `loadVideos()`, which builds a fresh pager from the first page. The current feed (mode or `?id=`) reloads with the new flag, without navigating away. The profile modal exists only on the home page (`index.html` / `videos.html`), so the video and search pages pick up the setting on their next request.\n\n**Files touched.** Engine:\n- `handlers/similar.py`\n- `request_context.py`\n- `server.py`\n- `recommendations/builder.py`\n- `data/metadata.py`\n- `data/random_videos.py`\n- `data/similarity_candidates.py`\n- `data/search.py`\n\nGateway:\n- `client/backend/server.py`\n\nFrontend:\n- `data/feed-params.ts`\n- `data/videos.ts`\n- `data/search.ts`\n- `pages/videos/index.ts`\n\nNo new files, and no new interfaces beyond the flag.\n\n### Alternatives considered\n\n- **Store the flag in `random-cache.db`.** Rejected. The cache is prebuilt and refreshed only on an interval, while `nsfw` in `whitelist.db` changes whenever the crawler or an `/api/video` refresh updates it. A cached flag would go stale and let a newly flagged video through until the next rebuild, breaking \"never sees\". The draw already joins `videos` in `fetch_metadata`, so reading the live flag costs nothing. Storing the flag would also need a schema change, a change to the `precompute-random-rowids` job, a forced rebuild of every deployed cache, and a reader for old caches.\n- **A data-layer default of \"filtered\".** Rejected. It would hide NSFW videos from `/api/video`, from internal like and block resolution, and from the ANN compute that writes the shared similarity cache. That breaks \"the video page plays whatever it is linked to\" and poisons the cache for visitors who opt in.\n- **Filtering inside the ANN compute, so cached similarity lists are NSFW-free.** Rejected. The cache is shared across requests, and with the filter off results must be identical to today's. Filtering has to happen after the cache is read (`_build_rows`), never before it is written.\n- **Passing the flag as an argument through `generate_recommendations` and every generator's `get_candidates`.** Rejected. It changes the Protocol and five generators plus two sources. The request context exists for exactly this kind of per-request value, and the builder already reads excluded keys from it through a dep.\n- **Folding the setting into the `feedParams:v1` object.** Rejected. `resolveFeedParams` skips storage when `?mode=` is present and returns only `{mode}`, and `chooseFeedMode` overwrites the object. The NSFW setting also applies to search and the video page, which never read feed params. A separate key keeps the two lifecycles apart.\n- **Reusing `_parse_bool` for the parameter.** Rejected. It accepts `true`, `yes` and `on`, and the requirement says only `1` includes NSFW.\n\n### Gotchas and risks\n\n- **The include default is a footgun.** A future listing call site that forgets to pass the flag would leak NSFW rows. Tests should pin each listing path (the five modes, `?id=` up-next, the video page's up-next, search, the random fallback and the vector path) against a fixture with `nsfw=1`, `0` and NULL rows, requested without the parameter.\n- **The existing suite relies on NULL flags.** `test_similar.py` compares the HTTP ordered feed, sent without `nsfw`, against `fetch_ordered_page` called at its default. That holds only because the fixtures leave `nsfw` NULL, which passes the filter. A fixture change adding `nsfw=1` rows would need the reference call to pass the flag.\n- **`RecommendationBuilderDeps` is frozen and built by keyword in tests.** The new field needs a default (the \"filtered\" callable) and must come last.\n- **Ordering and index cost.** The predicate makes the ordered and lexical queries walk further down their index to fill a page, in proportion to the NSFW share near the top of each order. The share was not measured, so the cost is unknown but bounded by the existing chunk and statement deadlines.\n- **The home change handler reloads through `loadVideos()`.** An in-flight `loadMoreVideos` already drops its result when the pager has changed (`current !== pager`), so no stale rows are appended.\n\n### Limitations (deliberate simplifications)\n\n- **The random cache refill is bounded at 4 draws.** If NSFW rows make up a very large share of the cache, a Random page can still come back short after four windows. The SQL fallback runs only when the cache returns nothing at all, which matches today's rule. Upgrade path: raise the cap, top up the shortfall from `fetch_random_rows`, or store a flag column in the cache once staleness is handled.\n- **The like layer can shrink per seed.** Each liked seed contributes up to `similar_per_like` rows (cache-limited), and NSFW rows among them are removed rather than replaced from that seed. The sources pool all seeds and truncate to the layer's fetch limit, so the layer usually stays full. A visitor whose likes sit in mostly NSFW neighbourhoods gets a smaller like layer, and the mixer's existing backfill fills those slots from other layers. The page is still full, but the layer ratio shifts for that visitor. Upgrade path: read deeper cache or ANN lists per seed when the filter is on.\n- **The vector half of search is not refilled.** NSFW hits are removed from the ANN rowid list rather than replaced, so the vector half can hold fewer than `candidate_pool` rows. Pages are much smaller than the fused pool, so only the tail of a long result set gets shorter. Upgrade path: overfetch the ANN search when the filter is on.\n\n### Tradeoffs the operator is asked to accept\n\n- **NULL flags pass the filter** (already decided). Any NSFW video the crawler has not flagged is shown to a filtered visitor.\n- **The data-layer default is include**, with the filtered default enforced at the request edge. This is safer for the video page and the shared cache, at the cost of the call-site discipline described under Gotchas.\n- **The setting is per browser only**, and the video and search pages have no control of their own; they read the stored value.\n- **Filter-on pages near the tail of a very NSFW-heavy pool** (random cache, like layer, search's vector half) can be shorter or differently mixed, within the bounds above. With the filter off, results are unchanged.\n</initial_solution>\n\n<conflicts>\nnone\n</conflicts>",
    "step_3_identify_impacts": "<impacts>\n\n<impacts>\n<impact path=\"engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py\" element=\"new module-level nsfw parser, next to _parse_int / _parse_bool / _parse_non_negative_int (lines 1126-1150)\">\n**What changes.** Add a pure helper, e.g. `_parse_include_nsfw(value: str | None) -> bool`. It returns True only for the exact string `\"1\"`. It returns False for None, `\"true\"`, `\"yes\"`, `\"on\"`, `\"01\"`, `\"0\"` and anything else. It must not reuse `_parse_bool` (1135-1139), which accepts `{\"1\",\"true\",\"yes\",\"on\"}` after `strip().lower()`.\n\n**Whitespace.** The plan does not say whether to strip, so choose and document it:\n- `parse_qs` (lines 479, 615) drops blank values, so `nsfw=` arrives as missing.\n- The gateway strips every value before forwarding (`client/backend/server.py:434, 489`), so a proxied `nsfw= 1 ` arrives as `1`.\n- Only a direct Engine call can present `\" 1\"`.\n\n**Depends on it.** `_handle_similar` and `_handle_search` (entries below), plus the new tests for \"only `1` includes\".\n\n**Regression risk: low.** It is new code. The trap is reusing `_parse_bool`, which would make `nsfw=true` leak NSFW rows.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py\" element=\"_handle_similar() (lines 994-1123): parse `nsfw` and store it in the request context\">\n**What changes.** Read `params.get(\"nsfw\", [None])[0]`, parse it with the new parser, and call the new setter from `request_context.py`.\n\n**Where to set it.** It must be set here, not in `_handle_similar_request`, because the GET alias `/videos/{id}/similar` reaches `_handle_similar` directly (`_dispatch_get`, lines 523-530) and never passes through `_handle_similar_request`.\n\n**Placement.** Put it next to `set_request_id(request_id)` (line 1035), preferably inside the `try` at 1037, so the `finally: clear_request_context()` at 1122-1123 clears it. The debug 403 (1018-1020) returns before that `try`. Setting the flag earlier would leave it uncleared on that path. This is harmless in practice because `SimilarServer` is a `ThreadingHTTPServer` (`server.py:14, 204`) with one thread per request, but it breaks the file's clear-what-you-set pattern.\n\n**Who reads it.** Every listing branch reached from here reads the flag:\n- `_handle_random` \u2192 `_fetch_random_rows`\n- `_handle_ordered_feed`\n- `_handle_home` (the mixer, through the builder dep, and its random fallback)\n- `_handle_seed_with_embedding`\n- the `seed.get(\"random\")` branch (1099-1108) \u2192 `_fetch_random_rows`\n- `_handle_vector_search`\n\n**Depends on it.** All the routes above. The `_DEBUG_CHILD` and `_FAILING_SIMILAR_CHILD` harnesses in `tests/active/test_similar.py` call `_handle_similar` on a `SimpleNamespace` server. The new setter only touches thread-local state, so those still run.\n\n**Regression risk: medium.** The data-layer default is include. Any branch that does not pass the flag through leaks NSFW rows silently, and no existing test notices.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py\" element=\"_fetch_random_rows() (lines 669-681) and its three callers: _handle_random (717-732), the empty-mix fallback in _handle_home (795-804), and the `seed.get('random')` branch of _handle_similar (1099-1108)\">\n**What changes.** Both draws get the flag:\n- `fetch_random_rows_from_cache(..., include_nsfw=...)` at line 671;\n- `fetch_random_rows(..., include_nsfw=...)` at line 677.\n\n**Where the flag comes from.** The plan does not say. Reading it from the request-context getter inside `_fetch_random_rows` is the safe choice. Adding a parameter to `_handle_random` is not: both test_similar harnesses replace `_handle_random` with a stub of the fixed signature `(self, limit, include_debug, request_id, started_at)` (`tests/active/test_similar.py:431, 541`). A fifth argument raises TypeError, which the handler turns into a 500. That would fail `test_debug_request_is_refused_403_unless_the_flag_is_set` and `test_recommendations_failure_answers_a_fixed_500_and_logs_its_traceback`.\n\n**Fallback rule.** The cache-then-DB rule (`if rows: return rows`) is unchanged. The SQL fallback runs only when the cache path returns nothing, which matches the plan.\n\n**Regression risk: medium.** This is the Random mode, the home empty-mix fallback and the random-seed path, all in one place.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py\" element=\"_handle_ordered_feed() (lines 734-779)\">\n**What changes.** Add `include_nsfw=...` to the `fetch_ordered_page` call (lines 751-757). With the predicate in the SQL:\n- `offset += chunk_size` (758) walks the filtered total order.\n- `len(chunk) < chunk_size` (770) now means the filtered order has ended.\n- NSFW rows no longer use up `ORDERED_FEED_MAX_CHUNKS` (107).\n\n`chunk_size` (745), the `exclude` and `seen` dedupe (759-766) and moderation (768) are unchanged.\n\n**Depends on it.** `tests/active/test_similar.py::_reference` (1062-1066) compares the HTTP pages against `fetch_ordered_page(..., error_threshold=threshold)` at the data-layer default (include). See the test_similar entry.\n\n**Regression risk: medium.** Filter-on pages differ from the reference whenever the live `whitelist.db` has `nsfw=1` rows inside `REFERENCE_DEPTH`.\n</impact>\n<impact path=\"engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py\" element=\"_handle_seed_with_embedding() (lines 813-933): UpnextPoolPolicy construction\">\n**What changes.** Pass `include_nsfw=<flag>` into `UpnextPoolPolicy(...)` (838-849). The flag comes from the context getter, or from a parameter. Nothing else here changes.     "step_4_reassess": "<summary>\nI checked the inventory against the code and it holds up. I opened `handlers/similar.py` (dispatch, `_handle_search`, `_handle_similar_request`, `_fetch_random_rows`, `_handle_ordered_feed`, `_handle_home`, `_handle_seed_with_embedding`, `_handle_vector_search`, `_handle_similar`, the parsers), `request_context.py`, `recommendations/builder.py`, `candidates/random_videos.py`, `data/random_videos.py`, `data/random_cache.py::fetch_random_rowids`, `data/db.py::swap_readonly_connection`, `data/similarity_candidates.py`, `data/search.py` and `data/metadata.py`. On the gateway and frontend side I opened the allowlist and both sanitisers in `client/backend/server.py`, and `feed-params.ts`, `videos.ts`, `search.ts`, `pages/videos/index.ts` (`loadVideos`, `loadMoreVideos`, `renderProfileSection`) and the likes page. The line numbers and behaviour matched every entry. That includes the inventory's three corrections to the plan: `WHERE` is built into `error_clause` in `fetch_random_rows`, `fetch_recent_videos` and `fetch_popular_videos`; `lexical_candidates` has no error clause; and `test_similar` reads the live `whitelist.db`. I also grepped every caller of the functions that gain the keyword, and every route in `_dispatch_get` and `do_POST`. No listing path gets around the design: the only video-list routes are `SIMILAR_POST_ROUTES`, the GET `/videos/{id}/similar` alias and `/api/v1/search/videos`. `fetchStaticVideosPayload` has no callers, the home `?id=` page never draws the seed as a card, and the personalisation rerank only reads embeddings, so it cannot add rows. The crawler and `/api/video` refresh both store `nsfw` as INTEGER 0/1/NULL (`schema.sql:53`, `video.py:312,409` writes a Python bool), so the predicate `v.nsfw IS NULL OR v.nsfw = 0` matches the stored values. the cache holds no NSFW flag, so allowed rows are found by redrawing.\nRANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS = 4\n\n\ndef fetch_random_rows_from_cache(\n    server: Any, limit: int, error_threshold: int | None = None, include_nsfw: bool = True\n) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Return random videos using the precomputed rowid cache; with the filter on, redraw windows until the page is full or the draws run out.\"\"\"\n    if server.random_cache_db is None or limit <= 0:\n        return []\n    draws = 1 if include_nsfw else RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS\n    seen: set[int] = set()\n    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n    for _ in range(draws):\n        # The handle is re-read under the lock on every draw: a refresh swap closes the old one once the lock is free.\n        with server.random_cache_lock:\n            rowids = fetch_random_rowids(server.random_cache_db, limit) if server.random_cache_db is not None else []\n        fresh = [rowid for rowid in rowids if rowid not in seen]\n        if not fresh:\n            break\n        seen.update(fresh)\n        with server.db_lock:\n            metadata = fetch_metadata(server.db, fresh, error_threshold=error_threshold, include_nsfw=include_nsfw)\n        for rowid in fresh:\n            meta = metadata.get(rowid)\n            if meta:\n                rows.append(meta)\n        if len(rows) >= limit:\n            break\n    return rows[:limit]\n```\n**Invariants of the loop:**\n- **Filter off equals today.** It makes one draw. `seen` is empty during the first draw, so a window is resolved exactly as today, duplicates included, and at most `limit` rows come back.\n- **Lock discipline.** The two locks are taken in turn, never nested, and the handle never lives across draws. It stops when widening finds no new hit above the floor.\n- **Side effect:** it also keeps widening past hits removed by exclude or moderation for filter-on requests. Fusion, `total` and slicing run over filtered lists.\n\n### 6. Gateway (`client/backend/server.py`)\n\n```python\n    \"/recommendations\": {\"id\", \"host\", \"limit\", \"random\", \"debug\", \"mode\", \"user_id\", \"nsfw\"},\n    \"/videos/similar\": {\"id\", \"host\", \"limit\", \"random\", \"debug\", \"mode\", \"user_id\", \"nsfw\"},\n    ...\n    \"/api/v1/search/videos\": {\"q\", \"page\", \"limit\", \"sort\", \"nsfw\"},\n```\nNothing else changes. The existing sanitiser strips values and drops blank ones, and forwards the rest with `urlencode`. The block and dislike row filter never looks at `nsfw`.\n\n### 7. Frontend\n\n**`data/feed-params.ts`**, appended after `readStoredFeedParams`. The module docstring changes to \"\u2026the home feed's parameters, and the NSFW setting every video list sends\". The `FeedParams` comment stays true, because the NSFW setting has its own key.\n```ts\n// The NSFW setting, kept apart from feedParams:v1: it applies to search and the video page too, and a ?mode= visit must not reset it.\nconst NSFW_FILTER_KEY = \"nsfwFilter:v1\";\n\n// Set on every change, so the choice holds on this page even when storage refuses the write.\nlet nsfwFilterInMemory: boolean | null = null;\n\n/**\n * Whether NSFW-flagged videos are hidden: true unless the visitor turned it off; missing, unreadable or corrupt storage means on.\n */\nexport function readNsfwFilter(): boolean {\n  if (nsfwFilterInMemory !== null) return nsfwFilterInMemory;\n  try {\n    return window.localStorage.getItem(NSFW_FILTER_KEY) !== \"off\";\n  } catch {\n    // Unreadable storage (private mode) keeps the filter on.\n    return true;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Turn the NSFW filter on or off for this page and, when storage allows, for later visits.\n */\nexport function setNsfwFilter(on: boolean) {\n  nsfwFilterInMemory = on;\n  try {\n    window.localStorage.setItem(NSFW_FILTER_KEY, on ? \"on\" : \"off\");\n  } catch {\n    // Ignore storage failures (quota/private mode): the in-memory value above still applies on this page.\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * The Engine's query entry for the NSFW setting: nsfw=1 only when the visitor turned the filter off.\n */\nexport function nsfwQuery(): [string, string][] {\n  return readNsfwFilter() ? [] : [[\"nsfw\", \"1\"]];\n}\n```\n**Storage values.** Only the exact string `\"off\"` turns the filter off; anything else, including a corrupt value, reads as on.\n\n**`data/videos.ts`.** The import becomes `import { feedParamsToQuery, nsfwQuery, type FeedParams } from \"./feed-params\";`. In `buildSimilarUrl`, after the `feedParams` block and outside it, so the `?id=` and video-page up-next calls without feed params are covered:\n```ts\n  for (const [key, value] of nsfwQuery()) url.searchParams.set(key, value);\n```\nThe flag is read on every URL build and never captured at page load.\n\n**`data/search.ts`.** It imports `nsfwQuery` and, after the `sort` line, adds `for (const [key, value] of nsfwQuery()) url.searchParams.set(key, value);`. The flag is on the URL before either branch, so the keyless cache key `search:${url}` separates on and off results.\n\nThe module comment is rewritten to: \"The gateway allowlists the route and exactly five query parameters (`q`, `page`, `limit`, `sort`, `nsfw`) and answers 400 for anything else, so this client sends those and nothing more; `nsfw=1` goes only when the visitor turned the NSFW filter off. A new filter needs the gateway updated in the same change.\"\n\n**`pages/videos/index.ts`.**\n- The import becomes `import { parseFeedMode, persistFeedParams, readNsfwFilter, resolveFeedParams, setNsfwFilter } from \"../../data/feed-params\";`.\n- New helper beside `profileActions`:\n```ts\n/**\n * The \"Hide NSFW videos\" checkbox, shown in every profile state; a change is saved in this browser and reloads the feed.\n */\nfunction nsfwToggle(): HTMLLabelElement {\n  const label = document.createElement(\"label\");\n  label.className = \"profile-nsfw\";\n  const input = document.createElement(\"input\");\n  input.type = \"checkbox\";\n  input.checked = readNsfwFilter();\n  input.addEventListener(\"change\", () => {\n    setNsfwFilter(input.checked);\n    void loadVideos();\n  });\n  label.append(input, \" Hide NSFW videos\");\n  return label;\n}\n```\n- `nsfwToggle()` is appended in each branch, just before `status`:\n  - issued-key view: `profileSection.append(warning, field, profileActions(copy, done), nsfwToggle(), status);`\n  - key-holding view: `profileSection.append(intro, profileActions(...), nsfwToggle(), status, blocks);`\n  - keyless view: `profileSection.append(intro, profileActions(create, resetLikesButton(status)), pasted, profileActions(use), nsfwToggle(), status);`\n- `renderProfileSection` rebuilds on every open, so the box always shows the current value.\n- **Stale-load guard in `loadVideos`.** This is outside the plan and closes the race the inventory found. A toggle during the first load, or during a `resetLikes` reload, must not render the older request's page:\n```ts\n    await localLikesImported;\n    const current = createFeedPager(fetchVideosPayload);\n    pager = current;\n    const payload = await current.next();\n    // A newer load (an NSFW toggle, a likes reset) replaced this pager; its own result renders instead.\n    if (current !== pager) return;\n```\n  The `catch` gets the same `if (current !== pager) return;` first, so the declaration moves above the `try`. Before the first await, `current` is the pager `loadVideos` created.\n- **`videos.css`.** One rule next to `.profile-actions`: `.profile-nsfw { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; margin: 0.75rem 0; }`.\n\n### 8. Check against the plan and the requirements (pass 1 of 3)\n\n| Requirement / plan item | Met by | Status |\n|---|---|---|\n| Visitor doing nothing never sees NSFW in any list | unset context reads as filtered; frontend sends nothing by default; every listing branch passes the flag (T10) | met |\n| Only `nsfw=1` includes | `_parse_include_nsfw`, exact match, no strip (T1) | met |\n| Filtering in the Engine, pages filled to size | SQL predicate inside the ordered, random, recent, popular and FTS queries; `_build_rows` skip before count; cache redraw; ladder keeps widening | met, with the limitations below |\n| Ordered paging neither skips nor repeats | predicate inside the ordered query; OFFSET walks the filtered order (T4) | met |\n| Up-next pool about 17 deep | `_build_rows` filter plus the filter-on stop rule (T8) | met up to the ANN caps |\n| Random full page; approach chosen and justified; cache schema unchanged | draw-time redraw, capped at 4; no rebuild | met up to the cap |\n| Filter off identical to today | every addition is gated on `include_nsfw=False`; the cache loop makes one draw; the ladder condition reduces to today's | met |\n| Browser and gateway never drop rows | only the allowlist changes; the frontend only adds a param | met |\n| Gateway allowlist on three routes | \u00a76 (T11) | met |\n| Setting in `localStorage` next to `feedParams:v1`; failures mean on; write failure keeps the choice for the page | \u00a77 feed-params (T12) | met |\n| Control only in the Profile modal, all three states, no key needed, reloads the home feed | `nsfwToggle` in three branches plus `loadVideos` (T13) | met |\n| Coverage: five modes, up-next (video page and `?id=`), search | `buildSimilarUrl` covers all feed and up-next calls; `fetchSearchResults` covers search | met |\n| Plan: data-layer default include; `/api/video`, `/internal/*` and the ANN compute untouched | defaults True; `ann.py` and `internal_client_reads.py` not edited | met |\n| Suite green | the three data-dependent tests are adjusted (\u00a71); `RecommendationBuilderDeps` default keeps `test_video.py` building; stubs keep their signatures | met in design; must be run |\n\nIt converged on this pass. Four places depart from, or add to, the plan text, and are named here:\n- **(a) The up-next ladder stop rule** changes for filter-on requests only. The plan asserts the ladder widens to `target_min_pool`, but the code did not guarantee that under the filter. Without the change the requirement's \"about 17 deep\" fails for NSFW-dense neighbourhoods.\n- **(b) The `loadVideos` stale-result guard.**\n- **(c) The shared `NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL` constant** in `metadata.py`, used in place of three copies of the literal.\n- **(d) The draw cap is its own constant, `RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS = 4`,** in the data layer. The plan said \"matching `ORDERED_FEED_MAX_CHUNKS`\", but that constant lives in a handler, and the data layer must not import from handlers.\n\n### 9. Limitations (deliberate simplifications, each with its ceiling and upgrade path)\n\n- **Random cache, 4 draws.** A cache that is mostly NSFW can still produce a short Random page. The SQL fallback runs only on an empty result. Upgrade: top up the shortfall from `fetch_random_rows`, or store a flag column once staleness is handled.\n- **Like layer.** NSFW neighbours are removed, not replaced per seed. The mixer's backfill keeps the page full, but the layer ratio shifts for NSFW-dense likes. Upgrade: read deeper per-seed lists when the filter is on.\n- **Search vector half.** No refill, so the tail of long result sets gets shorter. Upgrade: overfetch the ANN search when the filter is on.\n- **Raw-vector route (not in the plan's limitations).** A filter-on page is `limit` minus its NSFW hits. The frontend does not use this route. Upgrade: the same overfetch.\n- **Up-next ladder.** Under the filter it keeps widening only while ANN hits grow and stops at the caps. A seed whose whole reachable neighbourhood is NSFW (a filtered visitor opening an NSFW video by link) can still return a short page. This goes in `OVERVIEW.md` \u00a72.3.\n- **Refresh swap mid-refill.** A cache swap landing between two draws of one request can mix rowids from the old and the new file in one page. The rows are still valid, unfiltered-by-staleness videos. `test_random_cache` assumes no swap within a request.\n- **Checked-in `client/frontend/dist`.** It stays stale until it is rebuilt. Visitors would still be filtered by the Engine, but could not opt in.\n- **Likes page.** Liked NSFW videos stay visible there, through `/internal/videos/metadata`. It is outside the plan's coverage list; flagged as a scope question for the plan owner.\n\n</draft>",
    "step_6_develop_phase_breakdown": "<phases>\n<phase n=\"1\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>Seam: direct calls into the data layer on an in-memory sqlite db seeded with `nsfw` = 1 / 0 / NULL rows. This follows the existing `tests/active/test_random_videos.py` and `tests/active/test_metadata.py` harnesses. c1 is parametrized over the named functions (fetch_metadata, fetch_metadata_by_ids, fetch_random_rows, fetch_recent_videos, fetch_popular_videos, fetch_ordered_page, lexical_candidates), each with error_threshold on and off. It asserts that no returned row has nsfw = 1, that every NULL and 0 row the unfiltered call returns is still returned, and that the SQL runs in all four flag \u00d7 threshold combinations (this catches a `WHERE \u2026 WHERE`). fetch_metadata_by_ids is called on a multi-pair chunk with NSFW pairs in first, middle and last position, to cover the issue-33 parentheses rule, and fetch_metadata_by_uuids is shown to be unchanged. c2 puts NSFW rows at the top of the Hot, Recent and FTS-relevance orders and asserts three things: fetch_popular_videos(limit=n, include_nsfw=False) and lexical_candidates(limit=n, include_nsfw=False) each return n rows when at least n allowed rows exist; the concatenated fetch_ordered_page(offset=k*size, include_nsfw=False) pages equal one filtered page over the whole order, with no gap and no repeat; and search_videos `total` counts only allowed rows.</checkpoint>\n<name>SQL NSFW predicate in the data queries</name>\n<intent>With include_nsfw=False, the listing queries in data/metadata.py, data/random_videos.py and data/search.py apply NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL inside their SQL. NSFW-flagged rows are therefore gone before LIMIT and OFFSET are counted.</intent>\n<clause_1>With include_nsfw=False, fetch_metadata, fetch_metadata_by_ids, fetch_random_rows, fetch_recent_videos, fetch_popular_videos, fetch_ordered_page and lexical_candidates return no nsfw = 1 row and keep the NULL and 0 rows.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>With include_nsfw=False, the LIMIT and OFFSET of those queries count only allowed rows.</clause_2>\n<files>engine/server/data/metadata.py (EDITED), engine/server/data/random_videos.py (EDITED), engine/server/data/search.py (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n<phase n=\"2\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>c1 seam: fetch_random_rows_from_cache called on a SimpleNamespace owner (random_cache_db, random_cache_lock, db, db_lock), as `tests/active/test_random_cache.py` already does. The cache is built from rowids that mix NSFW and allowed videos, and the draws are counted by wrapping fetch_random_rowids. It asserts that include_nsfw=False fills `limit` across redraws, never makes more than RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS draws, stops after a draw adds no unseen rowid (a cache no bigger than `limit`), and returns [] on an all-NSFW cache. It also asserts that include_nsfw=True makes exactly one draw and returns that window's rows, duplicates included. c2 seam: a new unit test on get_upnext_candidates with a stub search_similar_above that records every (nprobe, search_limit) step and returns scripted hits, where one step's new hits are all NSFW. It asserts that under UpnextPoolPolicy(include_nsfw=False) NSFW entries do not reach the author cap or the count, that the ladder continues past the all-NSFW step while the raw hit count still grows, and that it stops at the caps. Under include_nsfw=True the recorded step and stop sequence must equal today's for the same script.</checkpoint>\n<name>Refill past NSFW rows outside SQL</name>\n<intent>With the filter on, the random-cache draw in data/random_videos.py and the up-next pool in data/similarity_candidates.py refill past NSFW rows instead of returning short. With the filter off, both behave as they do today.</intent>\n<clause_1>fetch_random_rows_from_cache(include_nsfw=False) keeps redrawing until one of three things happens: the page reaches `limit`, RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS draws have been made, or a draw adds no unseen rowid. With include_nsfw=True it makes exactly one draw.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>With include_nsfw=False, get_upnext_candidates drops NSFW entries before the author cap and before the count, and keeps widening the ANN ladder while the raw hit count still grows.</clause_2>\n<files>engine/server/data/random_videos.py (EDITED), engine/server/data/similarity_candidates.py (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n<phase n=\"3\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>Seam: the live `engine` and `client_backend` fixtures from `tests/active/conftest.py`, following the HTTP tests in `tests/active/test_similar.py` and `tests/active/test_server.py`. Rows are cross-checked against the set of keys that whitelist.db flags nsfw = 1, read through the `dataset` fixture. The test first asserts that this set is non-empty and that rows from it appear in the nsfw=1 responses, so the filter assertions cannot pass vacuously. c1 is parametrized over the listing paths: mode=recommendations, hot, recent, random and popular; id= up-next on POST /recommendations, POST /videos/similar and GET /videos/{id}/similar; random=1; the raw-vector path; and search. Each path is also parametrized over nsfw missing, empty, \"0\", \"true\" and \" 1\", and the test asserts that no returned key is in the flagged set. It sends mode=recommendations with nsfw=1 and then without it on the same Engine, which catches the builder freezing the flag at build time. c2 sends nsfw=1 through the gateway on /recommendations, /videos/similar and /api/v1/search/videos and asserts that the requests are forwarded (200, not 400) and that flagged rows can be returned. It also asserts that nsfw on /api/video is still a 400. The existing data-dependent tests are updated in the same phase, as the draft specifies: `_reference`, `ANN_CHILD` and `_seed_servable_cache`.</checkpoint>\n<name>Request edge, mixer wiring and gateway</name>\n<intent>An Engine listing request is NSFW-filtered unless it carries exactly nsfw=1. handlers/similar.py and request_context.py enforce this, and builder.py and server.py carry the flag into the mixer. client/backend/server.py forwards that opt-in on the three listing routes.</intent>\n<clause_1>A request to any listing path whose nsfw is anything other than exactly \"1\" receives no row that whitelist.db flags nsfw = 1.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>A gateway request carrying nsfw=1 on /recommendations, /videos/similar or /api/v1/search/videos reaches the Engine with the opt-in intact.</clause_2>\n<files>engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/request_context.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/server.py (EDITED), engine/server/api/recommendations/builder.py (EDITED), client/backend/server.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_similar.py (EDITED), tests/active/test_random_cache.py (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n<phase n=\"4\" kind=\"code\">\n<checkpoint>c1 seam: the bundled node harness of `tests/active/test_frontend_feed_params.py`, with in-memory localStorage. It asserts that storage values that are missing, \"on\", corrupt, or unreadable (getItem throws) read as filter on and add no nsfw param. Only \"off\" makes buildSimilarUrl (with and without feed params) and fetchSearchResults carry nsfw=1. When setItem throws, setNsfwFilter(false) still makes the next URL carry nsfw=1. c2 seam: a bundled DOM test like `tests/active/test_frontend_video_page.py` and `tests/active/test_frontend_profile.py`, with a stub fetch. The test is parametrized over the keyless, key-holding and issued-key profile states. It asserts that the checkbox is present and checked by default, and that changing it produces a feed request with the new nsfw value. The stub holds the first load's response and releases it after the toggle's response, and the test asserts that the rendered feed is the toggle's page.</checkpoint>\n<name>Browser NSFW setting and Profile control</name>\n<intent>The visitor's NSFW choice is held in the browser by data/feed-params.ts and decides whether the video-list requests in data/videos.ts and data/search.ts ask for NSFW rows. The home Profile modal in pages/videos/index.ts changes that choice and reloads the feed.</intent>\n<clause_1>buildSimilarUrl and fetchSearchResults add nsfw=1 only when the stored NSFW setting reads off.</clause_1>\n<clause_2>Changing the Profile-modal checkbox, in any of the three profile states, leaves the home feed showing the page fetched under the new setting.</clause_2>\n<files>client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts (EDITED), client/frontend/src/data/videos.ts (EDITED), client/frontend/src/data/search.ts (EDITED), client/frontend/src/pages/videos/index.ts (EDITED), client/frontend/src/pages/videos/videos.css (EDITED)</files>\n</phase>\n</phases>\n\n<needs_coordination>\nnone\n</needs_coordination>\n\n<rationale>\nThe build splits by layer, in the order dependencies run: data queries, then the refill mechanisms that sit outside SQL, then the request edge together with the gateway, then the browser. Each phase can be verified on its own because every data-layer keyword defaults to include=True. P1 and P2 therefore change no behaviour until P3 turns filtering on at the request edge, and P4 only adds a parameter the Engine already honours after P3. P1 and P2 are separate because the SQL predicate and the refill loops are different mechanisms with different seams: a sqlite fixture for P1, and draw counting with a stubbed ANN ladder for P2. Putting all of it in one phase would have needed four clauses. The gateway goes with the Engine edge rather than the frontend because its only job is to carry the opt-in to that edge, and it keeps P4 to two clauses: the setting and the control. The loadVideos stale-load guard is covered by P4 clause 2, since a stale page rendering would break \"the page fetched under the new setting\". \"Filter off is unchanged\" is not a separate clause. It is covered by the existing suite staying green, since those tests call at the include defaults, and by P2's assertions of one draw and an unchanged step sequence. There are no prose phases, because the only prose this build touches is documentation (OVERVIEW.md \u00a72.3), which Step 9 handles. Two things came up in this step. First, the {principles}, {shape_ladder-ladder} and {tdd_seams} slots in its prompt came through unfilled, so the seams were taken from the existing harnesses in tests/active. Second, P3's checkpoint depends on whitelist.db holding nsfw = 1 rows that the listing paths can reach, so it asserts that as a precondition rather than passing vacuously. The operator approved this plan.\n</rationale>",
    "author:tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py": "<assertions>\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:122 - for each of fetch_metadata, fetch_metadata_by_ids, fetch_random_rows, fetch_recent_videos, fetch_popular_videos and fetch_ordered_page hot/popular/recent, each at threshold None and 3: include_nsfw=True runs and returns the hand-derived set of all rows (E dropped under the threshold). Together with :124 this runs the SQL in all four flag \u00d7 threshold combinations - C1\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:124 - the same reads with include_nsfw=False return exactly the hand-derived allowed rows A,B,C,D,E (A,B,C,D under the threshold), in order for recent and the ordered pages. The id lookup gets its pairs with NSFW ones first (X1), in the middle (X3) and last (X4), so a predicate bound to one pair of the OR (the issue-33 rule) fails - C1\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:125 - no filtered row has nsfw = 1 - C1\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:126 - the filtered rows' nsfw values are exactly {0, None}, so both the 0 and the NULL rows stay - C1\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:133 - fetch_metadata_by_uuids at threshold None and 3 still returns every video including the four NSFW ones (unchanged) - C1\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:142 - with NSFW rows heading Hot (control :139), fetch_popular_videos(n, include_nsfw=False) returns the first n allowed rows for every n up to the allowed count, at threshold None and 3. A predicate on the outer query returns [] at n=1 - C2\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:143 - with NSFW rows heading Recent (control :140), fetch_recent_videos(n, include_nsfw=False) returns allowed[:n] in order for every n - C2\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:146 - fetch_random_rows(limit = allowed count, include_nsfw=False) returns every allowed row on each of five draws. A LIMIT counting NSFW rows passes one draw at best 1 in 70 - C2\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:155 - with an NSFW row heading each order (control :153), the single filtered fetch_ordered_page for hot/popular/recent at threshold None and 3 equals the hand-derived allowed order - C2\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:164 - filtered pages of size 1, 2 and 3 fetched at offset k*size, up to one past the end, repeat no row - C2\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:165 - those concatenated pages equal the single filtered page (no gap; OFFSET walks the filtered order past the mid-order NSFW row X3) - C2\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:214 - lexical_candidates (in the Engine-interpreter child) with include_nsfw=True runs and returns all nine matches in relevance order - C1\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:215 - lexical_candidates with include_nsfw=False returns exactly A,B,C,D,E in relevance order - C1\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:216 - no filtered lexical row has nsfw = 1 - C1\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:217 - the filtered lexical rows' nsfw values are exactly {0, None} - C1\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:231 - with NSFW rows heading FTS relevance (control :228), lexical_candidates(limit=n, include_nsfw=False) returns allowed[:n] for n = 1..5 - C2\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:232 - search_videos(include_nsfw=False) page 1 of 2 is A,B and total is 5, the allowed matches, against 9 unfiltered (control :229) - C2\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:233 - search_videos(include_nsfw=False) page 2 of 2 is C,D with total 5 - C2\ntests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py:234 - search_videos(include_nsfw=False) with candidate_pool=2 gives total 2 and rows A,B (a post-LIMIT drop would give total 0) - C2\n</assertions>\n\n<probes>\n1. ValidateTests [\"tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p1.py\", \"-s\"] (first version: imports and in-memory FTS5 bm25). It printed: test interpreter /home/enduser/code/PeerTube-browser/.pixi/envs/default/bin/python 3.14.7; \"data.search import failed ModuleNotFoundError No module named 'numpy'\", so the search reads have to run in a child on engine/.pixi's python; data.metadata and data.random_videos import in-process, and none of the signatures has include_nsfw yet; sqlite 3.53.4 builds an in-memory external-content fts5 table; bm25 order for 10-word titles with 9..1 \"cats\" is X1, X2, A, B, X3, C, D, E, X4, with scores around -2e-06/-1e-06 (idf is clamped because every doc matches, so tf still decides the order).\n2. ValidateTests [\"tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p1.py\", \"-s\"] (second version: the checkpoint's own _statements() fixture and READS, unfiltered). It printed: at threshold None every read returns all nine (recent, popular, and ordered hot/popular/recent in order X1,X2,A,B,X3,C,D,E,X4, with nsfw 1,1,0,None,1,0,None,0,1); at threshold 3 every read drops only E; fetch_popular_videos(1) and fetch_recent_videos(1) return ['X1'] at both thresholds; fetch_metadata_by_uuids returns all nine uuid keys (E dropped at threshold 3); ENGINE_PY exists; the child printed lexical(100) = X1..X4 in that same order with those nsfw values, lexical(1) = [X1], search page1/limit2/pool100 = rows X1,X2 total 9, page2 = A,B total 9, pool 2 = X1,X2 total 2. The probe file has been emptied to a one-line \"Delete this file\" note, following the repo's convention.\n3. ValidateTests [\"tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py\"]: 26 failed, 2 passed. Every failure is a TypeError \"unexpected keyword argument 'include_nsfw'\" from fetch_metadata, fetch_metadata_by_ids, fetch_random_rows, fetch_recent_videos, fetch_popular_videos, fetch_ordered_page or lexical_candidates (in the child), raised after that test's unfiltered controls had passed. The two passing tests are the fetch_metadata_by_uuids \"unchanged\" checks, which should be green before and after this phase.\n</probes>\n\n<unassertable>\nlexical_candidates has no error_threshold parameter (plan line 495 records this), so for it the seam's \"each with error_threshold on and off\" reduces to filter on and filter off with no threshold. Two further notes, neither a gap in C1 or C2: the tmp/ probe file tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p1.py is emptied but still exists, because no tool here deletes files; and the search reads run in a child on the Engine interpreter because the test interpreter has no numpy, so their failures show up as the child's stderr in the assertion message.\n</unassertable>",

The pool is then the observed unfiltered [X1, X2], and filtering it leaves {\"rows\": [], \"total\": 0}.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n</rows>\n\n<answers>\n1. Whole claim: yes, one fix. Every docstring claim has an assertion: the default and True reads at :121/:122/:213/:214; the exact filtered sets at :124/:215; no nsfw = 1 at :125/:216; {0, None} at :126/:217; NSFW pairs first, middle and last via PAIR_ORDER in _by_ids; uuid lookup unchanged at :133; LIMIT n at :142/:143/:231; five random draws at :146; paging at :155/:164/:165; search total and pages at :232-:234. The phase 1 checkpoint in docs/project/plans/22-36-nsfw-filter.md names search_videos `total` and fetch_metadata_by_uuids, so both are in scope. The fix: :133 was tagged `C1`, but fetch_metadata_by_uuids is not one of C1's reads and that assertion is green today. I relabelled it `# guard, no clause: fetch_metadata_by_uuids is outside the filter and stays unchanged`. It has no row.\n2. Absence only: no. Each \"no nsfw = 1 row\" assertion (:125, :216) is armed by an unfiltered control that returns the four NSFW rows (:121, :213) and paired with an exact positive equality (:124, :215). Each LIMIT/OFFSET check has a control showing an NSFW video heads that order (:139, :140, :153, :228) and one showing the unfiltered total of 9 (:229).\n3. Echoed literal: no. Every expected value is a hand-written constant (EXPECTED, or the literal rows and totals at :232-:234), not computed by any production call. _ranked only sorts labels for reads whose order is not their contract. The production line whose deletion turns these red is the `(v.nsfw IS NULL OR v.nsfw = 0)` predicate the phase adds to each query's WHERE (inside popular_ids for fetch_popular_videos, and in lexical_candidates' FTS query), plus search_videos passing include_nsfw to lexical_candidates. Deleting the predicate lets X1-X4 back in at :124/:125/:215/:216, and deleting the pass-through reads total 9 at :232.\n4. One value: no. Each read runs at thresholds None and 3 and with the flag at default, True and False. nsfw takes the values 1, 0 and NULL. LIMIT runs at every n from 1 to the allowed count, and pages at sizes 1, 2 and 3. :164/:165 compare pages against `whole` from the same function, but `whole` is itself pinned to the hand-derived allowed list at :155.\n5. The double: no. The child's server is a SimpleNamespace(db, db_lock, query_encoder=None). search_videos reads it only through search_connection's fallback (getattr search_db -> None, so server.db and server.db_lock), getattr statement_timeout_seconds, and vector_candidates' getattr query_encoder. It carries the real connection and a real lock and stands in for no project logic. query_encoder=None is the real degrade-to-lexical path (search.py:179-181).\n6. It collects: yes. The run collected 28 = 8 reads \u00d7 2 thresholds + 2 uuid + 2 limits + 3 orders \u00d7 2 thresholds + 1 lexical + 1 search, which matches the file. The `--collect-only -q` summary line reads \"no tests\" because that runner counts outcomes, not collected ids. It exited 0, and the full run below reports 26 failed and 2 passed, with no collection or import error. Every keyword used (error_threshold, limit, offset, order name) exists on the real signatures; the unfiltered calls ran green.\n7. Observed, not predicted: yes for everything that can be run today. The unfiltered orders for all eight reads at both thresholds passed at :121. The heads of Hot, Recent and each ordered page passed at :139/:140/:153. The child's unfiltered search output was never printed in the checkpoint run because the child died on the second call, so I probed it this turn (tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p1.py, emptied again). The probe printed lexical(100) = [['X1', 1], ['X2', 1], ['A', 0], ['B', None], ['X3', 1], ['C', 0], ['D', None], ['E', 0], ['X4', 1]], lexical(1) = [['X1', 1]], search page 1 = {'rows': [['X1', 1], ['X2', 1]], 'total': 9}, page 2 = {'rows': [['A', 0], ['B', None]], 'total': 9}, and pool 2 = {'rows': [['X1', 1], ['X2', 1]], 'total': 2}. That confirms the controls at :213/:228/:229 and the row shape [video_id, nsfw]. The filtered expecteds cannot be observed until include_nsfw exists. They are the observed unfiltered orders with the nsfw = 1 labels removed, and the implementation run will confirm them.\n8. Red, not green: yes, it fails. ValidateTests on tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase1.py printed \"26 failed, 2 passed\" with exit status 1. The 2 passing are the fetch_metadata_by_uuids guard at :133 (both thresholds), which asserts behaviour this phase must keep and carries no clause.\n9. Red for the right reason: yes. Every failure is the missing keyword, the one thing phase 1 adds, and every control before it passed. test_the_filter_drops_every_nsfw_row_... fails at :122 with \"TypeError: fetch_metadata() got an unexpected keyword argument 'include_nsfw'\" (via :85), and the same for fetch_metadata_by_ids (:90), fetch_random_rows (:97), fetch_recent_videos (:98), fetch_popular_videos (:99) and fetch_ordered_page (:100-:102), after :121 passed. test_limits_count_only_allowed_rows fails at :142 with \"TypeError: fetch_popular_videos() got an unexpected keyword argument 'include_nsfw'\", after the controls at :139/:140 passed. test_filtered_pages_... fails at :154 with \"TypeError: fetch_ordered_page() got an unexpected keyword argument 'include_nsfw'\", after :153 passed. Both search tests fail at :199 `assert proc.returncode == 0` with the child's stderr \"TypeError: lexical_candidates() got an unexpected keyword argument 'include_nsfw'\". That is the child's call carrying the flag, not a harness fault: the probe shows the same child running every unfiltered call to exit 0.\n10. Observed expected output: every expected value the run could reach matches what it printed. The unfiltered controls passed at :121/:139/:140/:153, and the probe printed the child values quoted in 7 (relevance order equal to ORDER, head X1, unfiltered total 9, unfiltered pool-2 rows X1/X2). The run contradicted nothing. The filtered expecteds (allowed lists and totals of 5 and 2) are derived by hand from those observed orders; they were not seen and cannot be until the phase exists.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:1": "<changes>\n### engine/server/data/metadata.py\n- New module constant `NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL = \"(v.nsfw IS NULL OR v.nsfw = 0)\"`. Its comment says why NULL passes: only rows the crawler flagged `nsfw = 1` are left out. `random_videos.py` and `search.py` import it, so the rule is written in one place.\n- `fetch_metadata` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True` after `error_threshold`. With the filter on, `AND NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL` goes on the line after `{error_clause}`, in every 900-rowid batch.\n- `fetch_metadata_by_ids` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True` and passes it through `_select_pairs` to `_select_metadata`. Both helpers take `include_nsfw: bool = True` as their last parameter. `_select_metadata` puts the same `nsfw_clause` after `{error_clause}`. Because the pair OR is already in parentheses, the clause applies to every pair in the chunk. The comment there now names both clauses.\n- `fetch_metadata_by_uuids` is unchanged. It gets the helpers' default of True, so `/internal/*` lookups still return NSFW videos.\n- At the default, parameters and rows are the same as before; the SQL text gains only a blank line.\n\n### engine/server/data/random_videos.py\n- Imports `NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL` from `data.metadata`.\n- `fetch_random_rows`, `fetch_recent_videos` and `fetch_popular_videos` each gain `include_nsfw: bool = True`. Each now builds its WHERE from the `conditions` list that `fetch_ordered_page` already used: the error condition, then `NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL` when the filter is on, joined with AND. This means the error and NSFW conditions can't produce two WHERE clauses.\n- With the filter off, the rendered WHERE and the params are the same as before: `[threshold, limit]` or `[limit]`, and `[threshold, limit, limit]` or `[limit, limit]` for popular.\n- In `fetch_popular_videos` the `{where_clause}` sits inside the `popular_ids` subquery, where `{error_clause}` was, so that subquery's `LIMIT` counts only allowed rows.\n- `fetch_ordered_page` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True` and adds `NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL` to its conditions after the recent-order condition, so `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` walk the filtered order.\n- `fetch_random_rows_from_cache` is untouched. The redraw loop belongs to a later phase.\n\n### engine/server/data/search.py\n- Imports `NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL` from `data.metadata`.\n- `lexical_candidates` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True`, which is also documented in its docstring. With the filter on, `AND NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL` goes on the line after `WHERE videos_fts MATCH ?`, so the FTS `LIMIT` counts only allowed matches. The params tuple is unchanged.\n- `vector_candidates` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True` and passes it to `fetch_metadata`, so the vector half drops NSFW rows too.\n- `search_videos` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True` after `vector_weight` and passes it to both halves. Fusion, `total` and page slicing then work on lists that are already filtered.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

C2\n</assertions>\n\n<probes>\nProbe file tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p2.py, run as ValidateTests [\"tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p2.py\", \"-s\"] and [\"tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p2.py\", \"-s\", \"-k\", \"ladder\"]; output read from tests/last_test_output.txt:\n- The test interpreter is .pixi/envs/default/bin/python 3.14.7. `numpy missing No module named 'numpy'` and `faiss missing No module named 'faiss'`, so data.ann cannot be imported here; replacing it in sys.modules with a stub search_similar_above works, and get_upnext_candidates ran through it.\n- Today's get_upnext_candidates, author cap 1, target 5, LADDER script (X1 .95 ch-X, A .9; +X2 .85; +Y .8 ch-X; +B .78, C .76): calls [(1,10),(2,20),(4,40)], stats steps [(1,10,2),(2,20,3),(4,40,3)], rows ['X1','A','X2'], tail 0.\n- Today's result with the step-2-adds-nothing script (author cap 0): calls [(1,10),(2,20)], steps [(1,10,2),(2,20,2)], rows ['X1','A'].\n- Today's result with the one-step CAPPED script (top_k 3, target 3, cap 1): calls [(1,10)], steps [(1,10,3)], rows ['X1','X2','B'].\n- Today's fetch_random_rows_from_cache over the window A X1 A E(errored), limit 4, threshold 3: rows ['A','X1','A'], and randint was called once as (0, 4) (total 8 - limit 4).\n- A 3-row cache at limit 5: randint was never called (offset-0 window) and rows were ['X1','A','X2'].\n- The real checkpoint, run with ValidateTests [\"tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase2.py\"]: 11 failed, 1 passed. Every failure is `TypeError: ... unexpected keyword argument 'include_nsfw'` (fetch_random_rows_from_cache / UpnextPoolPolicy) or `AttributeError: ... no attribute 'RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS'`, never setup. The checkpoint also prescribes this seam (\"a stub search_similar_above that records every step\"). random_cache.random is stdlib and is scripted. fetch_random_rowids is wrapped as a spy, and the real function still runs.\n6. Every helper argument exists on the real types: fetch_random_rowids(cache_db, limit), fetch_metadata(db, rowids, error_threshold), UpnextPoolPolicy fields, and search_similar_above(server, seed, nprobe, search_limit, min_score). The only names not yet present are the phase's own new surface: the include_nsfw keyword and RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS.\n7. Yes, observed. Probes under tests/tmp ran the test's own helpers. With today's code they gave: LADDER unfiltered ([(1,10),(2,20),(4,40)], [X1,A,X2], [(1,10,2),(2,20,3),(4,40,3)]); STALLED ([(1,10),(2,20)], [X1,A], [(1,10,2),(2,20,2)]); CAPPED ([(1,10)], [X1,X2,B], [(1,10,3)]); cache windows OVERLAP [[X1,A,X2,B],[X2,B,C,X3],[C,X3,D,E]] and SMALL [[X1,A,X2],[X1,A,X2]]; ALLNSFW today [X1,X2,X3,X4]; and cap windows reproduced exactly for caps 3 and 5. The filtered expected values beyond those can only exist after the phase lands. They follow from the clause over inputs the probes confirmed. The probe file is now reduced to a docstring and should be deleted; I have no delete tool.\nNothing rewritten; no self-check answer was yes.\n8. Yes, it fails. The one pass is test_filter_off_makes_one_draw_and_returns_its_rows_duplicates_included[default]. It checks today's behaviour under the default flag, and it is meant to stay green.\n9. It shows the wrong implementation producing different values on 100/101/188/189/190. On 203-205 and 219-220 it produced the same filtered values as expected; those lines exclude the other wrong implementations named in the rows (always-widen, post-cap filtering).\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:2": "<changes>\n### engine/server/data/random_videos.py\n- New constant `RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS = 4`, placed after the imports. It caps the filter-on draws per request. It is kept separate from `ORDERED_FEED_MAX_CHUNKS` because the data layer must not import from handlers.\n- `fetch_random_rows_from_cache` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True`. It now draws in a loop: `1` draw when `include_nsfw` is True, `RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS` when it is False.\n  - On each draw, `server.random_cache_db` is read again under `random_cache_lock`, so the handle is never kept from one draw to the next (a refresh swap closes the old handle once the lock is free). The rowids already seen are dropped, and the loop stops at the first draw that adds none.\n  - The new rowids are resolved with `fetch_metadata(..., include_nsfw=include_nsfw)` under `db_lock`. The two locks are never held together.\n  - Rows are appended in draw order. The loop stops once the page reaches `limit`, and the result is cut to `limit`.\n- With the filter off it makes one draw, and `seen` is empty during that draw. That draw's window resolves as it does today, duplicates and rows short from `error_threshold` included.\n\n### engine/server/data/similarity_candidates.py\n- `UpnextPoolPolicy` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True`, after `refresh_cache`.\n- `_build_rows` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True` and passes it to both `fetch_metadata_by_ids` calls, with and without the lock. An NSFW entry then finds no metadata and is skipped before the author cap and before the `limit` count.\n- `_upnext_rows` passes `policy.include_nsfw` to `_build_rows`. Cached entries and ANN fallback hits are filtered at the same point.\n- The ladder in `get_upnext_candidates` records `hits_before` on each step. The stop rule is now `len(rows) <= before and (policy.include_nsfw or len(hits) <= hits_before)`: with the filter on, a step that adds no row still widens while the raw ANN hit count grows. With the filter off the condition is the same as today's. The ladder is still bounded by `max_nprobe`/`max_search_limit`.\n- The `get_upnext_candidates` docstring now mentions the NSFW filter and the new widening rule.\n\n### Not done in this phase\nThe plan's code sketch also adds `SimilarityCandidatesPolicy.include_nsfw` and passes `policy.include_nsfw` from `get_similar_candidates` to `_build_rows`. Neither this phase's intent nor its checkpoint covers that, so I left it out. Phase 3's builder wrapper (`replace(policy, include_nsfw=...)`) needs it, and Phase 3's files list does not name `similarity_candidates.py`. So Phase 3 will have to make that two-line change as an unanticipated file, or the change needs to be assigned to a phase.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nnone\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "author:tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase3.py": "<items>\n<item id=\"C1c\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>Added test_a_gateway_listing_request_without_exactly_nsfw_1_gets_no_flagged_row_where_nsfw_1_gets_some, which runs over the three gateway routes (POST /recommendations?mode=recent, POST /videos/similar?mode=recent, GET /api/v1/search/videos?q=hentai) \u00d7 the five NSFW_VALUES (missing, empty, \"0\", \"true\", \" 1\"). For each case it first sends the same route through the gateway with nsfw=1 and asserts at least one flagged key (:130, the control). Then it sends the non-\"1\" value through the gateway and asserts 200 with rows (:95 via _keys, and :132) and no flagged key (:134). The operator was asked whether the gateway leg should cover \" 1\", given the plan's value-stripping (plan lines 155 and 540). The answer was \"cover-space-1\", so \" 1\" is sent. Each wrong gateway fails :134 on a flagged row: one that strips nsfw before forwarding (\" 1\" \u2192 \"1\"), one that normalises \"true\" \u2192 \"1\", and one that forwards nsfw=1 whenever the key is present (\"0\", \"true\", \"\" and \" 1\" all fail). A gateway that refuses non-\"1\" values fails :95. A pass-through that is actually unfiltered is ruled out by the :130 control.</what>\n</item>\n<item id=\"D13\">\n<disposition>justified</disposition>\n<what>I narrowed the docstring's closing paragraph to what the test sends: \"Every Engine request carries its own X-Client-IP, and every gateway request its own X-Forwarded-For.\" It now says outright that the resolved-address forwarding is not asserted here and points to the test that does assert it: tests/active/test_server.py::test_engine_receives_the_resolved_address_as_x_client_ip (:414\u2013436). That test records the x-client-ip an Engine stub receives and asserts [\"203.0.113.9\", \"203.0.113.9\", \"127.0.0.1\", \"127.0.0.1\"].</what>\n</item>\n<item id=\"N1c\">\n<disposition>fixed</disposition>\n<what>I took mode=popular out of LISTINGS and deleted UNREACHABLE and the :104 skip branch. test_a_listing_request_without_exactly_nsfw_1_gets_no_flagged_row_where_nsfw_1_gets_some now covers only the 10 armed listings, and every parametrization runs the nsfw=1 control at :110 that the name promises. Popular has its own test, test_a_popular_request_without_exactly_nsfw_1_gets_rows_and_no_flagged_row (:118\u2013123). Its name claims only rows and no flagged row, so it no longer claims the \"where nsfw_1 gets some\" control. It carries the operator's existing C1 popular exemption, and its comment and the docstring bullet both say it passes whatever the filter does.</what>\n</item>\n</items>\n\n<findings_addressed>\nClaim CRITICAL 1 (non-\"1\" nsfw never sent through the gateway): added the gateway \u00d7 five-value test at :126\u2013134, with an nsfw=1 control at :130 and a no-flagged-row assertion at :134. The operator ruled that \" 1\" is covered (\"cover-space-1\"). Consequence for the implementation step: the plan's gateway change was allowlist-only and relied on the existing strip (plan :155/:540). That no longer passes. Phase 3 must forward nsfw unstripped, or drop any value other than exactly \"1\", and the plan's gateway paragraph needs to match. Probe run today: all 15 new cases fail at :95 on the control's 400 {\"error\": \"Unknown query parameter: nsfw\"}, and the 5 popular cases pass.\nClaim RECOMMENDATION 1 (D13) taken: the docstring is narrowed and points to tests/active/test_server.py::test_engine_receives_the_resolved_address_as_x_client_ip.\nClaim RECOMMENDATION 3 (N1c) taken: popular is split into its own test, so the armed test's name holds for every one of its ids.\nClaim RECOMMENDATIONS 2, 4 and 5 not taken. For 2: the isolation this test relies on is asserted in test_server.py, and engine_client's gateway limiter is RateLimiter(100000, 60).\n</findings_addressed>\n\n<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase3.py:114, armed by :110. For the 10 Engine listings (mode recommendations with 5 flagged likes, hot, recent, random; up-next on POST /recommendations, POST /videos/similar and GET /videos/{id}/similar; random=1; vector; search q=hentai) \u00d7 nsfw missing/empty/\"0\"/\"true\"/\" 1\", no returned key is flagged, on every draw (12 for the random feeds, 3 for mixed). :113 asserts the page is non-empty, and :110 asserts the same path with nsfw=1 served at least one flagged key on the same Engine first.</assertion>\n<expected>Every page is 200 with rows, and set(keys) & flagged is empty.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>Each of these fails :114 with flagged keys listed: an unfiltered handler (today, 50 of 50 fail there); a presence-only check (\"0\"); a truthy parse via _parse_bool (\"true\"); a strip or int parse (\" 1\"); and a mixer flag frozen True at build, or cached from the preceding nsfw=1 request. A flag frozen False fails :110 instead, and a handler that empties filtered pages fails :113.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase3.py:134, armed by :130. Through the Client backend in front of the session Engine, POST /recommendations?mode=recent, POST /videos/similar?mode=recent and GET /api/v1/search/videos?q=hentai, each with nsfw missing/empty/\"0\"/\"true\"/\" 1\", return no flagged key. :132 asserts rows are present, and :130 asserts the same gateway route with nsfw=1 served at least one flagged key first.</assertion>\n<expected>200 with rows, and set(keys) & flagged is empty for all 15 cases.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>Each of these fails :134, because recent's sixth row is flagged, and so are 19 of 20 gateway search hits: a gateway that strips nsfw before forwarding, as the existing sanitiser does at server.py:434/:489 (\" 1\" arrives as \"1\"); one that maps \"true\" to \"1\"; and one that forwards nsfw=1 whenever the key is present. A gateway that answers 400 on non-\"1\" values fails :95.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase3.py:123. mode=popular \u00d7 the five values returns 200 with rows (:122) and no flagged key.     "self_check:tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase3.py": "<rows>\n<row clause=\"C1\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase3.py:115 \u2014 `assert not set(keys) & flagged`. It runs against the session Engine on 10 listing paths: mode=recommendations with five flagged likes, hot, recent and random; up-next for a flagged seed on POST /recommendations, POST /videos/similar and GET /videos/{id}/similar; random=1; the raw-vector POST /recommendations; and search q=hentai. Each path is sent with nsfw missing, empty, \"0\", \"true\" and \" 1\", drawn 12 times for the random feeds and 3 times for the mixed feed. Before each, the line 111 control proves the same path with nsfw=1 serves at least one flagged key on the same Engine, and line 114 proves the filtered page is non-empty. The flagged set comes independently from whitelist.db read-only.</assertion>\n<expected>Under the right implementation, every filtered page is non-empty and shares no key with the whitelist.db nsfw = 1 set, while the nsfw=1 request before it still serves flagged rows.
