For example, recent-missing showed [('c90660f2-\u2026', 'peertube.boooks.lol')] and upnext GET /videos/{id}/similar-missing showed 810video.com keys.</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A handler that doesn't read nsfw and serves the unfiltered listing, which is today's code: line 115 reads a non-empty intersection, as the run showed. A handler that filters only when nsfw is missing but treats \"0\", \"true\", \"\" or \" 1\" as an opt-in (truthy parse or strip) fails on those parametrizations. A handler that filters always, ignoring the opt-in, fails the line 111 control. A mixer whose flag is frozen at build time serves the same filtered or unfiltered page to both requests, so either line 111 or line 115 goes red. A handler that answers filtered requests with no rows fails line 114.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase3.py:123 \u2014 POST /recommendations?mode=recent, POST /videos/similar?mode=recent and GET /api/v1/search/videos?q=hentai&limit=100, each with &nsfw=1, go through a real Client backend wired to the session Engine and must answer 200 with a rows dict. Line 124 then requires at least one key of that page to be in whitelist.db's nsfw = 1 set. Line 127 requires the same request without nsfw to answer rows with no flagged key, so the flagged rows at 124 come from the forwarded opt-in.</assertion>\n<expected>Under the right implementation, 200 with rows at 123, at least one flagged key at 124, and a non-empty page with no flagged key at 127. Against the code as it stands, the run showed line 123 failing on all three routes with ('/recommendations', 400, {'error': 'Unknown query parameter: nsfw'}) and the same for /videos/similar and /api/v1/search/videos. The run never reached lines 124 and 127. Their expectation rests on the Engine-direct run: recent and search with nsfw=1 served flagged rows (control line 111 passed), and without nsfw they served them too (line 115 failed).</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A gateway that still refuses nsfw answers 400 at 123, which is today's code, as the run showed. A gateway that allowlists nsfw but drops it from the forwarded query, or rewrites it to something other than \"1\", gets the Engine's filtered page, so 124 reads an empty intersection. A gateway that forwards nsfw=1 unconditionally, for example by hard-coding it, serves flagged rows on the plain request, so 127 reads a non-empty intersection.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n</rows>\n\n<answers>\n1. Whole claim: yes for one sub-case, now handled by exemption. Every docstring bullet has an assertion: the non-empty flagged set (fixture line), 11 paths \u00d7 5 values (line 115), the nsfw=1 control per path (line 111), the gateway opt-in and plain requests (lines 123/124/127), and /api/video (line 134). But the docstring itself concedes that mode=popular's check passes whatever the filter does, so C1 isn't carried for popular at this seam. I put that to the operator with AskUser. They approved keeping popular as an exempted smoke check (see exemptions), and the UNREACHABLE comment now says so. One mislabel: line 134 (/api/video still refused) claimed C2, but C2's text doesn't cover it and it's green before the phase. I relabelled it \"scope guard\", so it has no row.\n2. Absence only: for the 10 reachable paths, no. The negative at line 115 is armed by the nsfw=1 control at line 111 on the same path and Engine, and by the non-empty check at line 114. The negative at line 127 is armed by line 124. For mode=popular, yes: there's no control, because its first flagged row sits at position 2650, beyond what the feed can reach. That is the case the operator exempted rather than a rewrite. Line 134's 400 is armed by the 502 control at line 132.\n3. Echoed literal: no. C1 is read at five non-\"1\" values across ten paths plus one opt-in value. C2 is read on three routes with and without the opt-in. The random feeds get 12 draws and the mixed feed 3.\n5. The \"no tests\" shown in the collect-only summary is validate_tests.py's phrase() printing an empty outcome summary, not a collection failure.\n7. The 400 body at line 123 was seen in the run. Not observed: lines 124 and 127 through the gateway after the phase, because the gateway refuses nsfw today and the run stops at 123. What would confirm them is the phase's own green run. Their premise, that recent and hentai search serve flagged rows with nsfw=1, was observed Engine-direct in this run. The probe tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p3.py is already emptied to a docstring; I have no delete tool, so it still needs removing.\nRewrite made: the gateway opt-in's status check was inside the shared `_keys` helper (old line 95), so the first run's gateway red landed on a harness precondition shared with every Engine request. I also relabelled line 134 as a scope guard and noted the popular exemption on the UNREACHABLE comment. I then re-answered 1\u20137 over the new file, as above.\n8. Red, not green: yes. ValidateTests printed \"53 failed, 6 passed \u2026 recorded: tests/last_test_validation.json (exit 1)\", with exit status 1. The 6 passes are mode=popular \u00d7 5 (the exempted smoke check) and test_the_gateway_still_refuses_nsfw_on_api_video (the scope guard, green before the phase as it should be).\n9. Red for the right reason: yes. All 50 Engine failures are \"tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase3.py:115: AssertionError\", the C1 assertion. Each failed on flagged keys in a page served without exactly nsfw=1, for example recent-missing: [('c90660f2-31fd-4577-a25f-cd0e78406556', 'peertube.boooks.lol')]. Observed expected output: C1's expected column states what the run showed today (line 111 passes, line 115 fails with flagged keys) and what it must read after the phase. C2's line 123 expectation is the observed 400 today and 200 after. Lines 124 and 127 were not reached, and the row says so and names the Engine-direct observation they rest on. The run contradicted no expected value.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\n<exemption clause=\"C1\">\n<answer>Approve</answer>\n<why>This concedes only the mode=popular parametrization of C1 (LISTINGS entry \"mode=popular\", UNREACHABLE on line 44, and its runs through line 115).     "step_7_implement:3": "<changes>\n### engine/server/api/request_context.py\n- New `set_request_include_nsfw(value)` / `fetch_request_include_nsfw()` pair, following the `excluded_keys` pattern. When nothing was set, the getter returns False (filtered), so any path that never sets the flag stays filtered.\n- `clear_request_context` also clears `include_nsfw`. Its docstring now lists everything it clears.\n\n### engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py\n- New `_parse_include_nsfw(value)`, placed beside `_parse_bool`. It returns True only for the exact string `\"1\"` and does not strip. It does not reuse `_parse_bool`, which also accepts `true`, `yes` and `on`.\n- `_handle_similar` sets the flag as the first statement inside its existing `try`, so the `finally: clear_request_context()` clears it. It reads only `params`, so the SimpleNamespace test harnesses and the four-argument `_handle_random` stubs are unaffected.\n- The listing branches read the flag from the request context:\n  - `_fetch_random_rows` passes it to both `fetch_random_rows_from_cache` and `fetch_random_rows`. This covers Random, `random=1`, the home empty-mix fallback and the random-seed branch.\n  - `_handle_ordered_feed` reads it once and passes it to `fetch_ordered_page`, so OFFSET walks the filtered order.\n  - `_handle_seed_with_embedding` puts it on `UpnextPoolPolicy(include_nsfw=...)`.\n  - `_handle_vector_search` passes it to `fetch_metadata`. A `rat-tail:` comment records that flagged hits are dropped, not refilled.\n- `_handle_search` never enters `_handle_similar`, so it parses `nsfw` itself and passes `include_nsfw=` to `search_videos`.\n\n### engine/server/api/recommendations/builder.py\n- `RecommendationBuilderDeps` gains `fetch_include_nsfw: Callable[[], bool] = lambda: False`. It is the last field and has a default, so the keyword construction in `tests/active/test_video.py` still builds.\n- The four `*_filtered` closures (random, random-cache, recent, popular) pass `include_nsfw=deps.fetch_include_nsfw()` on every call, not once at build time.\n- New `get_similar_candidates_filtered` wrapper. It uses `replace(policy, include_nsfw=...)` and falls back to `SimilarityCandidatesPolicy()` when the policy is None. It is handed to both `AnnSimilarFromLikesDeps` and `CachedSimilarFromLikesDeps`, so both the like source and its fallback are filtered.\n- Imports `replace` and `SimilarityCandidatesPolicy`.\n\n### engine/server/api/server.py\n- Imports `fetch_request_include_nsfw` and wires it in as `fetch_include_nsfw=` on `RecommendationBuilderDeps`.\n\n### engine/server/data/similarity_candidates.py (unanticipated, see below)\n- `SimilarityCandidatesPolicy` gains `include_nsfw: bool = True`.\n- `get_similar_candidates` passes `policy.include_nsfw` to `_build_rows`, with a comment that the cache written before it stays unfiltered.\n\n### client/backend/server.py\n- `\"nsfw\"` is added to `PROXY_ALLOWED_QUERY_PARAMS` for `/recommendations`, `/videos/similar` and `/api/v1/search/videos`. `/api/video` still refuses it with a 400.\n- New `PROXY_UNSTRIPPED_QUERY_PARAMS = frozenset((\"nsfw\",))`. Both proxy sanitisers (GET and POST) forward `nsfw` without stripping it; every other parameter is still stripped.\n  - This departs from the plan, which said the existing sanitiser needed no change. Stripping would turn `\" 1\"` into the opt-in at the gateway, and the checkpoint's gateway ` 1` case forbids that.\n  - Now the value is URL-encoded as-is (`+1`) and the Engine alone decides whether it is exactly `1`. Empty values are still dropped by `parse_qs`, so they reach the Engine as missing (filtered).\n\n### tests/active/test_similar.py\n- `_reference` calls `fetch_ordered_page(..., include_nsfw=False)`, because the HTTP pages it is compared with carry no `nsfw` and are now filtered (Recent's sixth row is flagged). The module docstring bullet and the helper docstring say so.\n- `_vector_page` sends `&nsfw=1`, and the module docstring says so.\n  - This departs from the draft, which had `ANN_CHILD` pass `include_nsfw=False` and loosened the check to `len <= VECTOR_LIMIT`. That would have weakened the nprobe control.\n  - I observed that the filtered music-seed page is 95 rows (one flagged hit), while with `nsfw=1` it is 96. With the opt-in the route stays a pure ANN search, so `ANN_CHILD` and the strict `== VECTOR_LIMIT` check are unchanged.\n\n### tests/active/test_random_cache.py\n- The `_seed_servable_cache` seeding query also requires `(v.nsfw IS NULL OR v.nsfw = 0)`, so it keeps matching what the random feed serves to a request without `nsfw`. I checked the 20 rowids it currently picks: all have `nsfw = 0`, so the seeded set does not change.\n\n### Observed with probes (not the checkpoint)\n- `linux` and `cooking` up-next still fill 48, 30 and 8 rows with no flagged row.\n- `q=music&limit=20` still returns 20 rows, and home `{}` still returns 48 rows in mode `home`.\n- `mode=recommendations` with flagged likes serves flagged rows with `nsfw=1` and none without it or with `nsfw=true`, alternating on the same Engine.\n- Gateway `mode=recent`: `nsfw=1` gives 1 flagged row. Missing, `%201` and `true` give none, each on a full 48-row page.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nengine/server/data/similarity_candidates.py: `SimilarityCandidatesPolicy.include_nsfw` plus passing `policy.include_nsfw` into `_build_rows` in `get_similar_candidates`. Without it, the builder's like-layer wrapper (`replace(policy, include_nsfw=...)`) raises TypeError and the mix's like layer serves flagged rows. The Phase 2 outcome already recorded this gap. It is two lines.\ntests/tmp/test_probe_36_p3_impl.py: my throwaway probe, which ends in a deliberate `assert False`. I have no delete tool, so it needs deleting by hand.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",

It renders whichever response resolves last and shows peer.example::uuid-a1..a3.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>test_36_nsfw_filter_phase4.py:329 \u2014 checking the box again sends exactly one more feed request, with no nsfw.</assertion>\n<expected>[{\"mode\": [\"recommendations\"], \"nsfw\": []}]</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A handler that always calls setNsfwFilter(false), or ignores input.checked, sends nsfw [\"1\"] again. A handler that reloads only on uncheck sends no request, so the list is [].</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n<row clause=\"C2\">\n<assertion>test_36_nsfw_filter_phase4.py:330 \u2014 after re-checking, the feed shows the third page.</assertion>\n<expected>[\"peer.example::uuid-c1\", \"peer.example::uuid-c2\", \"peer.example::uuid-c3\"]</expected>\n<wrong_implementation>A change handler that saves and requests but leaves the old cards rendered (for example, a reload whose result is discarded). The feed still shows peer.example::uuid-b1..b3.</wrong_implementation>\n</row>\n</rows>\n\n<answers>\n1. Whole claim: I found one gap and rewrote it. The docstring said the first feed request is \"POST /recommendations\", but the stub records only mode and nsfw, so the method was never asserted. It is not part of C2, so I changed the docstring line to \"is to /recommendations\". The profile states and the held first request are covered by the controls at :318 and :319, and \"released and read\" by the control at :325.\n2. Absence only: no. Each also has a positive in the same run: the \"off\" case at :250 for :259, :253 for :256, :271 for :272, :274 for :276 and :323 for :329.\n3. Echoed literal: no. The expected nsfw values are constants and the production code builds the URLs. _keys builds \"host::uuid\", which is video-card.ts's key format. That format was observed in a probe (the release rendered peer.example::uuid-a1..a3), and what discriminates is which page (a/b/c) renders. The lines whose deletion turns each assertion red: `for (const [key, value] of nsfwQuery()) url.searchParams.set(...)` in buildSimilarUrl and search.ts (:250/:254); `nsfwFilterInMemory = on` in setNsfwFilter (:271/:276); `if (current !== pager) return;` in loadVideos (:327); `void loadVideos()` in nsfwToggle (:323/:329).\n4. One value: no. C1 is read over 11 stored or unreadable states, on both search branches, and through set/reload sequences. C2 is read in three profile states and in both toggle directions.\n5. The double: no. The doubles are fetch (network), a recording DOM (browser), and in-memory localStorage/sessionStorage (browser storage). These are all severed layers. videos.ts, search.ts, feed-params.ts and pages/videos/index.ts are the real modules, bundled with esbuild.\n6. It collects: yes. The run printed \"collected 6 items\": three data tests plus the home test \u00d7 3 profile states = 6, which matches what I wrote. The pre-run collect-only summary said \"no tests\", but the actual run collected all six. Every name resolves: _esbuild, _case, _run, _nsfw, _rows, _keys, PROFILE_STATES and the fixtures.\n7. Observed: I ran two probes under tests/tmp/ with the test's own runners on the current code.\n - Home probe: in all three states, feedAtStart was [{\"mode\": [\"recommendations\"], \"nsfw\": []}] and heldAtStart was true. The intros were \"No profile. \u2026\", \"This browser holds a profile key.\" and \"This is the only copy of your key. \u2026\". afterOff cards were [] while the first page was held. After release, cards were [\"peer.example::uuid-a1\", \"peer.example::uuid-a2\", \"peer.example::uuid-a3\"] and firstBodyRead was true, with no rejections. This confirms the hold/release harness and the _keys format.\n - Data probe: keyed was {'off': [False], 'off-keyed': [True], 'missing': [False], 'reload': [False, False]}, and all URL controls passed, including over a reload.\n - Not observable before the phase exists: the nsfw == [\"1\"] value and the checkbox/set paths, since there is no setNsfwFilter and no checkbox yet. The [\"1\"] form follows the list shape getAll was seen to return ([]) and the plan's `searchParams.set(\"nsfw\", \"1\")`. Running the phase's implementation would confirm it.\n - Both probe files were emptied, since I have no delete tool. tests/tmp/probe_36_home_harness.py and tests/tmp/probe_36_data_harness.py should be removed.\n8. Red, not green: yes, it is red. ValidateTests exited 1 with \"tests/tmp/test_36_nsfw_filter_phase4.py  6 failed\".\n9. Red for the right reason: yes.\n - test_only_a_stored_off\u2026 fails at :250, a C1 assertion, not a control: \"AssertionError: [{'bare': [], 'feed': [], 'search': [], 'keyed': False}] \u2026 {'feed': []} != {'feed': ['1']}\". The _run controls at :226-228 passed for every case, including the getItem-throws case.\n - test_set_nsfw_filter_holds\u2026 and test_set_nsfw_filter_is_read_back\u2026 fail at :223: \"('empty', 'TypeError: m.feedParams.setNsfwFilter is not a function \u2026runner.mjs:28:51')\" and the same for 'persist'. setNsfwFilter is the phase's own new export (plan \u00a77, feed-params.ts), so it is missing because the phase is not built, not because of a typo. In the 'empty' case the read before the set ran and passed its URL controls.\n - All three home cases fail at :321, a C2 assertion: \"AssertionError: ([], [])  assert [] == [{'checked': True}]\". The controls at :318 and :319 passed in every state.\n10. Observed expected output: every row's expected matches the run where the run reached it. :250 reads [] now and [\"1\"] is expected under the implementation. :321 reads [] now. :327's key format and release path were observed as the a-page keys in the probe. Rows past the first failing line in each test (:254-:259, :271-:284 and :323-:330) were not reached in this run. Their expected values rest on the observed shapes named in 7, and I have not claimed them as seen.\n</answers>\n\n<exemptions>\nnone\n</exemptions>",
    "step_7_implement:4": "<changes>\n### client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts\n- Module docstring now also names the NSFW setting every video list sends.\n- New key `NSFW_FILTER_KEY = \"nsfwFilter:v1\"`, stored apart from `feedParams:v1`, plus a module-level `nsfwFilterInMemory: boolean | null`.\n- `readNsfwFilter()`: the in-memory choice if one was set this page; otherwise `true` unless storage holds exactly `\"off\"`. A missing, corrupt or unreadable value (getItem throws) reads as on.\n- `setNsfwFilter(on)`: sets the in-memory value, then tries to store `\"on\"`/`\"off\"`, ignoring a storage failure the same way `persistFeedParams` does. So the choice still holds on the current page when setItem throws.\n- `nsfwQuery()`: returns `[[\"nsfw\", \"1\"]]` when the filter is off, `[]` otherwise.\n\n### client/frontend/src/data/videos.ts\n- Imports `nsfwQuery`. `buildSimilarUrl` adds its entries after the `feedParams` block and outside it, so the `?id=` up-next feed and the video page's up-next feed (both called without feed params) carry `nsfw=1` too. The value is read each time a URL is built, never captured at page load.\n\n### client/frontend/src/data/search.ts\n- Imports `nsfwQuery` and adds its entries after the `sort` line, before the keyed/keyless branch. Both branches send the flag, and the keyless cache key `search:${url}` keeps filtered and unfiltered results apart.\n- The module comment now lists five gateway-allowed parameters (`q`, `page`, `limit`, `sort`, `nsfw`) and says `nsfw=1` goes only when the filter is off.\n\n### client/frontend/src/pages/videos/index.ts\n- Imports `readNsfwFilter` and `setNsfwFilter`.\n- New helper `nsfwToggle()`, next to `profileActions`. It builds a `label.profile-nsfw` holding a checkbox, checked unless the filter is off, and the text \" Hide NSFW videos\". Its `change` handler calls `setNsfwFilter(input.checked)` then `loadVideos()`.\n- `renderProfileSection` adds `nsfwToggle()` just before `status` in all three branches: issued-key, key-holding and keyless.\n- Stale-load guard in `loadVideos`: the pager is created and assigned (`const current = \u2026; pager = current;`) before the `try`. After `await current.next()`, and first thing in the `catch`, it returns if `current !== pager`. A newer load (an NSFW toggle or a likes reset) therefore wins over an older request that resolves later.\n\n### client/frontend/src/videos.css\n- One rule after `.profile-actions`: `.profile-nsfw { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; margin: 0.75rem 0; }`.\n</changes>\n\n<inner_tests>\nnone\n</inner_tests>\n\n<unanticipated>\nclient/frontend/src/videos.css - the phase lists `client/frontend/src/pages/videos/videos.css`, but that file doesn't exist. The home page imports `../../videos.css`, which is `client/frontend/src/videos.css`, so the plan's one `.profile-nsfw` rule went there.\n</unanticipated>\n\n<awaiting_operator>\nnone\n</awaiting_operator>",
    "step_8_i1_refactor": "<refactors>\nengine/server/data/random_videos.py: added `_listing_conditions(error_threshold, include_nsfw)`. It returns the error-threshold condition and the NSFW condition, plus their params, which `fetch_random_rows`, `fetch_recent_videos`, `fetch_popular_videos` and `fetch_ordered_page` each used to build in a copied 7-line block. All four now call it; `fetch_ordered_page` then appends its recent-order condition. The params order is unchanged ([threshold, now_ms, ...limit/offset]) because the NSFW condition takes no param. The only difference is that in the recent order's WHERE the NSFW term now comes before the date term; AND order does not change the result.\n</refactors>\n\n<left_out>\nThe one-line `nsfw_clause = \"\" if include_nsfw else f\"AND {NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL}\"` still appears in 3 places (metadata.fetch_metadata, metadata._select_metadata, search.lexical_candidates). A shared helper would save one line per place and make readers look it up in a second module, so it isn't worth it.\nThe GET and POST proxy sanitisers in client/backend/server.py still repeat the query loop, now including the `PROXY_UNSTRIPPED_QUERY_PARAMS` line. That duplication predates this build, and merging them means changing how both return their 400s, which is more than this feature needs.\nThe lock/no-lock pair of `fetch_metadata_by_ids` calls in similarity_candidates._build_rows was already there; the phase only added an argument to each, so I left the structure alone.\nThe large SELECT column lists repeated across metadata.py, random_videos.py and search.py are also pre-existing and outside this feature.\nThrowaway files I can't delete (I have no delete tool), which need removing by hand: tests/tmp/test_probe_36_refactor_equivalence.py and its tests/tmp/probe_36_refactor_snapshot.json, plus Phase 3's tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p3_impl.py, which ends in a deliberate `assert False`.\nThe pass template's `{rat_tail_rules}` placeholder was empty, so I checked the pass against the role's own rule instead: the one new `rat-tail:` comment, on the vector-search path in similar.py, names its limit and its upgrade path.\n</left_out>\n\n<needs_fresh_red>\nnone\n</needs_fresh_red>\n\n<observation>\nBefore the change I captured a snapshot probe on the Phase 1 fixture: the 3 fetchers plus fetch_ordered_page for hot, popular and recent, at error threshold none and 3 and include_nsfw true and false, with an extra future-dated row and an undated row. After extracting `_listing_conditions`, the same probe gives identical rows and order in every combination.\n</observation>",
    "step_8_triage:0": "<failures>\n### tests.active.test_frontend_upnext_pager::test_the_pager_s_48_row_batches_never_repeat_a_row_and_it_stops_asking_after_an_empty_batch\n**Symptom.** The pager's second batch (`calls: 2`, a POST `/recommendations?id=\u2026&host=\u2026&limit=48` with the first batch's 48 rows as `exclude`) came back as a 500 `{\"error\": \"Recommendations request failed\"}` from the Engine.\n\n**The test.** It is sound: it drives the real Client and Engine and only needs requests that should succeed to succeed. Its premise still holds with the NSFW filter on (no `nsfw` is sent). Run in isolation through its own `_run`/`_seed` harness, it gave `[48, 48, 48, 48, 48, 48, 12, 0, 0, 0]`, exactly what its docstring and `_seed` comment describe. It does not conflict with any confirmed requirement of this build, so it is not retired.\n\n**The implementation.** No build defect was found; see the shared cause below. Nothing was changed.\n\n### tests.active.test_server::test_a_keyed_request_s_500_entry_exclude_reaches_the_engine_and_none_of_it_is_returned\n**Symptom.** The keyed home request with 500 `exclude` entries was answered 500 `{\"error\": \"Recommendations request failed\"}`. The two keyed requests before it, without `exclude`, were answered 200.\n\n**The test.** It is sound, for the same reasons. Replayed in isolation (5 likes, 4 dislikes, one previous page, then exclude sizes 48, 100, 200, 300 and 500), every request returned 200 with 48 rows. It is not retired.\n\n**The implementation.** No build defect was found. Nothing was changed.\n\n### Shared cause (observed mechanism; the trigger in the suite run is not directly observed)\n- **Only one path gives this exact body.** `SIMILAR_FAILED_MESSAGE` is returned only by `_handle_similar`'s `except ValueError` (for a non-bad-request text) and `except Exception` (engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py:1126-1134).\n- **A statement timeout ends up there.** POSTs run under a 5 s wall-clock `statement_deadline` (`DEFAULT_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5.0`). When it trips, sqlite raises `OperationalError: interrupted`. The broad `except Exception` catches it before `do_POST` can turn it into 503 `Query time limit exceeded`.\n- **Observed with a lowered budget.** I started an Engine with `server_config` overridden, the same way `CACHE_VARIANT_RUNNER` does:\n  - At a 0.05 s budget, the up-next-with-exclude request, the keyed home with 500 excludes and `mode=hot` with exclude each returned exactly this 500. The Engine logged `server error \u2026 sqlite3.OperationalError: interrupted` (from `fetch_metadata` under `search_similar_above`, from `fetch_random_rows_from_cache` and from `fetch_ordered_page`).\n  - At a 0.3 s budget, up-next (about 0.2 s) passed and home (about 0.8 s) still returned 500.\n- **The build did not make these requests slow.**\n  - `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` for the pair query is identical with and without `NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL`: MULTI-INDEX OR on `sqlite_autoindex_videos_1`. There is no nsfw index and none is needed.\n  - `_select_pairs` over 1,350 pairs took 0.045 s unfiltered and 0.039 s filtered.\n  - Over HTTP, averaged over 3 runs: up-next with 48 excludes took 0.20 s filtered and 0.19 s with `nsfw=1`. Home with 5 likes and 500 excludes took 0.79 s filtered and 0.69 s with `nsfw=1`.\n  - Phase 2's widened ladder does not run here: the linux seed's first ANN step already yields 252 rows (204 after 48 excludes), above the pool target.\n- **Load slows these requests.** Replaying the two requests while 8 Engines start at once (as `test_engines_starting_at_once_all_become_healthy` does in the `test_random_cache.py` lane) pushed home from about 0.8 s to 2.06 s. That did not reach 5 s: the probe was rate-limited to about 60 real requests and did not have the other 19 lanes' load. The failing run had 20 lanes, including test_similar (90 s) and test_random_cache (67 s, which also starts variant Engines).\n- **Not confirmed.** The Engine logs of the failing run (pytest-6302 and pytest-6305) had already been removed by pytest's basetemp retention, so I could not see the actual exception. The same generic handler would also turn any other load-dependent sqlite error, such as `database is locked` on a file another lane's Engine writes, into this same 500.\n- **What would confirm it.** In the next red run, read the failing lane's `engine0/engine.log` for the `server error` record and check whether it ends in `OperationalError: interrupted`.\n\n**Conclusion.** These are load-dependent failures of correctly written tests, made worse by a masking bug that predates this build. They are not a regression of the NSFW work, as far as I could measure.\n</failures>\n\n<checkpoint_gaps>\nnone. I found no implementation fault from this build for a checkpoint to have missed. The filter's measured cost on both failing paths is 0.01 to 0.1 s against a 5 s budget. Mapping a statement timeout to 500 instead of 503 predates this build (`_handle_similar`'s broad `except Exception`), and no phase of this build was asked to change it.\n</checkpoint_gaps>\n\n<correction>\nNo implementation or test file was changed, and no test was retired. Neither red test conflicts with a confirmed requirement of this build, and neither passes vacuously: the pager still returns 48\u00d76, 12, then empty with the filter on, and the keyed exclude request still returns a full 48-row home page. No checkpoint was touched.\n\nActions taken:\n1. I read both failing tests and confirmed they are correctly built.\n2. I replayed each one in isolation through probes, and both passed.\n3. I found the only code path that returns their exact 500 body. With a lowered statement budget I showed that a timed-out statement lands on that path, as `OperationalError: interrupted`.\n4. I measured the filter's cost with plans, in-process timings and HTTP timings, filter on against `nsfw=1`, and found it negligible.\n5. I measured how much 8 concurrently starting Engines slow the home request: from 0.8 s to 2.06 s.\n\nRecommended next step: re-run the suite. If either test goes red again, read that lane's `engine0/engine.log` for the `server error` record before its temp dir is recycled. If it shows `OperationalError: interrupted`, the fix is outside this build's approved scope. Either catch the interrupt in `_handle_similar` (engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py), so it gets the existing 503 and a timeout stops posing as a server fault, or reduce lane contention. It should be filed in `docs/project/issues/` rather than absorbed here.\n\nFiles outside the step: my throwaway probe `tests/tmp/test_probe_step8_exclude_500.py` is now emptied to a docstring so it cannot start Engines, but I have no delete tool, so it needs deleting by hand. Phase 3's `tests/tmp/test_probe_36_p3_impl.py` is still pending deletion too. My `ValidateTests` probe runs rewrote `tests/last_test_validation.json` and `tests/last_test_output.txt` with the probe's own results. The workflow's next `--compare` run should regenerate both.\n</correction>",
    "step_9_triage": "<docs>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/README.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe Notes section has no `nsfw` bullet, so the Engine's listing contract is incomplete: today every listing request without an exact `nsfw=1` is filtered. Add a bullet beside the `mode`/`debug`/`seed` bullets (lines 26-28). It should say that `nsfw` on POST `/recommendations`, POST `/videos/similar`, `GET /videos/{id}/similar` and GET `/api/v1/search/videos` includes NSFW-flagged videos only for the exact, unstripped value `1` (`_parse_include_nsfw`). Missing, empty, ` 1`, `true`, `yes`, `0` or any other value filters them. Only rows with `videos.nsfw = 1` are removed; NULL and 0 pass. The bullet should list the coverage: every feed mode (recommendations mix including the like layer, hot, recent, random, popular), the random=1 alias and the empty-mix fallback, up-next, the raw-vector route and search. It should note that the raw-vector route drops flagged hits without refilling, so its page can be short. Name the exceptions: `/api/video`, `/api/video/refresh` and `/internal/*` are never filtered. Also point to OVERVIEW.md for how pools refill. Line 9, which says `/api/video` returns `nsfw`, stays true.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"client/README.md\" update=\"yes\">\nLine 28 says any query parameter not on a route's allowlist answers 400. Line 25's gateway filtering description names only blocks and dislikes. Nothing says `nsfw` is allowed. Add a bullet after line 28 saying that `nsfw` is on the allowlist for `/recommendations`, `/videos/similar` and `/api/v1/search/videos` (and still refused with 400 on `/api/video`). Unlike every other parameter, it is forwarded without stripping (`PROXY_UNSTRIPPED_QUERY_PARAMS`), so only an exact `1` opts in at the Engine. An empty value is dropped and reaches the Engine as missing, which means filtered. The Engine does the NSFW filtering for keyed and keyless requests alike, so it is separate from the gateway's block and dislike row filter and its over-fetch.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"client/frontend/README.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThere is no NSFW setting in \"What it does\". Add a bullet for it:\n- it is stored in `localStorage` under `nsfwFilter:v1` as `on`/`off`, separate from `feedParams:v1`;\n- only an exact `off` turns the filter off; missing, corrupt or unreadable storage means on, and if a storage write fails the choice still holds for the current page;\n- its only control is the \"Hide NSFW videos\" checkbox (`label.profile-nsfw`) in the Profile modal, in the keyless, key-holding and just-issued-key states, with no key needed;\n- changing it on the home page reloads the feed, and an older in-flight load that finishes later is discarded;\n- home feed requests in every mode, up-next (the home `?id=` view and the video page, through `buildSimilarUrl`) and search (`fetchSearchResults`) send `nsfw=1` only when the filter is off, reading the value each time a request is built;\n- the video and search pages have no control of their own.\n\nLine 12 says `feed-params.ts` is the one module for feed parameters; widen it to cover the NSFW setting and `nsfwQuery`. Line 8's list of gateway routes leaves out `/api/v1/search/videos`, which the search page calls; add it.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md\" update=\"yes\">\nSeveral sections describe how pools are built but not the NSFW filter:\n- **Section 1 (lines 9-18).** Unless the request carries `nsfw=1`, every mode and up-next leave rows with `nsfw = 1` out while the pool or page is built. For hot, recent and popular the predicate is in the ordered query, so the paging walk (line 34) steps through the filtered order and flagged rows do not count against the chunk cap.\n- **Random (line 11).** Describe the filter-on draw. It makes up to `RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS` (4) cache windows, drops rowids already seen, and stops when the page is full or a window adds no new rowid. It falls back to the DB draw only when the result is empty.\n- **Line 35.** \"Random is not filtered\" is about `exclude`. Reword it, for example \"Random does not apply `exclude`\", so it is not read as covering NSFW.\n- **Section 2.3 (lines 47-54).** Add NSFW to the list of filters on line 48, applied before the pool is counted and before the author cap. On line 49, the stop rule is different with the filter on: a step that adds no visible row still widens the search while the raw ANN hit count grows, and stops only at the target, at the caps, or when the hits stop growing. The checklist had expected the opposite (that a step adding only NSFW hits would stop the ladder), so write the rule as delivered.\n- **Similarity cache (item 3).** The ANN compute and the cache write stay unfiltered, so the shared cache serves both settings, and filtering happens only when rows are built.\n- **Section 3.** On the exploit layer, the like-derived candidates are filtered through both the ANN and the cached source. On random/explore, point to the redraw.\n- **Section 4.** A note may say that a like neighbourhood with many NSFW videos can shift the layer ratio.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/LAYER_PARAMS.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe \"Random Cache Params (Global)\" section (lines 128-138) and the explore and random \"Source\" lines (76, 114) describe the cache without saying how it relates to the NSFW filter. Say that the cache stores only rowids and holds no NSFW flag. The flag is read from `whitelist.db` when the rows are resolved at draw time. With the filter on, a draw makes up to `RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS` = 4 windows (`engine/server/data/random_videos.py`) to fill the page, and takes each lock separately on every window. No rebuild or migration is needed for the filter. The up-next constants section could add that with the filter on, the fallback keeps widening past steps that add only flagged hits, still bounded by `SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_NPROBE`/`SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"CONTEXT.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe glossary has no term for the filter. Add **NSFW filter**: a per-browser setting, on by default and stored in `localStorage`, not on the profile. It makes the Engine leave `videos.nsfw = 1` rows out of every video listing (feeds, up-next, search). A visitor opts out by sending `nsfw=1`, and unflagged (NULL) videos pass. It is separate from a Block, a dislike and operator moderation, and a video page opened directly is never filtered. The Block entry (line 11) could mention it among the things it is separate from.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"DEPLOYMENT.md\" update=\"no\">\nNothing it says has become false. Record the decisions and outcomes under Comments:\n- no per-mode toggles (Q1);\n- coverage: all five feed modes, up-next and search; not `/api/video` or `/internal/*`; channels unaffected (Q2);\n- stored in `localStorage` only, under `nsfwFilter:v1`, persisting across reloads (Q3, Q4);\n- no warning on a directly opened NSFW video page (Q5);\n- NULL passes, chosen without a measurement;\n- the random cache is unchanged, the flag is read at draw time with up to 4 redraws, and no rebuild is needed;\n- only an exact `nsfw=1` opts in.\n\nAlso record the open scope question from the impact inventory: the likes page still shows liked NSFW videos, because it resolves through the unfiltered `/internal/videos/metadata`.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/PIPELINE_DIAGRAM.md\" update=\"yes\">\nThe diagram lists the filters on each pool, and those lists are now incomplete. Node S (line 46, \"Similarity candidates filters: seed exclude, error_threshold, max_per_author, exclude_source_author\") and node U2 (line 67, \"Pool filters: tail floor, seed, error, author caps, request exclude, moderation\") should include NSFW (unless `nsfw=1`). A note or a node after `Request /recommendations` (line 8) could say that `nsfw` is parsed into the request context and that every candidate source applies the NSFW predicate.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"docs/project/adr/\" update=\"yes\">\nAdd a new ADR, `0007-nsfw-filter-default-at-request-edge.md`. It records that the data-layer functions default to `include_nsfw=True` and that the filtered default is enforced at the request edge: `_handle_similar` and `_handle_search` parse `nsfw`, the request-context getter returns False when unset, and `RecommendationBuilderDeps.fetch_include_nsfw` defaults to False. Its reasons: `/api/video`, the `/internal/*` like, block and import resolution (`fetch_metadata_by_uuids` and the ids path), and the shared similarity cache (`ann.compute_similar_items`) must stay unfiltered. It should also record the rule that follows: any new listing path must pass the flag, because the data layer leaks by default. The ADR directory holds 0001-0006 and none of them covers this.\n</doc>\n<doc path=\"client/frontend/src/data/search.ts\" update=\"no\">\nPhase 4 already rewrote the module comment (lines 4-8). It now names five gateway-allowed parameters (`q`, `page`, `limit`, `sort`, `nsfw`) and says `nsfw=1` goes only when the filter is off, which matches the delivered code.\n</doc>\n</docs>\n\n<adr_conflicts>\nnone\n</adr_conflicts>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/README.md": "<changes>\nAdded an `nsfw` query-parameter bullet to the Notes section of `engine/server/README.md`, after the `seed` bullet.\n\n- **Routes and parsing:** the bullet covers POST `/recommendations`, POST `/videos/similar`, `GET /videos/{id}/similar` and GET `/api/v1/search/videos`. Only the exact, unstripped value `1` includes NSFW-flagged videos (`_parse_include_nsfw`). A missing or empty value, ` 1`, `true`, `yes`, `0` or anything else filters them.\n- **What is removed:** only rows with `videos.nsfw = 1` are left out. NULL and `0` pass (`NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL`).\n- **Coverage:** every feed mode (including the mix's like layer), the `random=1` alias and the empty-mix fallback, up-next, the raw-vector route and search. For how each pool refills, the bullet points to OVERVIEW.md.\n- **Short pages:** the raw-vector route drops flagged hits without refilling, so its page can be short.\n- **Never filtered:** `/api/video`, `/api/video/refresh` and `/internal/*`.\n- **Unchanged:** line 9 (`/api/video` returns `nsfw`) is still true.\n\nI checked all of this against the code:\n- `GET /videos/{id}/similar` goes through `_handle_similar`.\n- `_handle_search` parses `nsfw` itself.\n- Blank values are dropped by `parse_qs`, so an empty value arrives as missing.\n\nOne problem I found but did not fix, since it is outside this file: the `_parse_include_nsfw` docstring in `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py` still says \"the gateway strips before forwarding\". Phase 3 made the gateway forward `nsfw` without stripping, so that sentence is out of date.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:client/README.md": "<changes>\nAdded a gateway bullet in `client/README.md` for the `nsfw` query parameter: which routes allow it, that it is forwarded unstripped, and how it differs from block/dislike filtering.\n\n- New bullet after the `mode` bullet (Backend Responsibilities). It says `nsfw` is allowed on `/recommendations`, `/videos/similar` and `/api/v1/search/videos`, and that `/api/video` refuses it with 400. Checked against `PROXY_ALLOWED_QUERY_PARAMS` in `client/backend/server.py`.\n- It says `nsfw` is the one parameter forwarded without stripping (`PROXY_UNSTRIPPED_QUERY_PARAMS`, used in both the GET and POST sanitisers), so the Engine alone judges the value. An empty value is dropped and reaches the Engine as missing (`parse_qs` plus the `if value:` guard).\n- Which values opt in (exact `1`) is linked to `engine/server/README.md`, which owns that contract, rather than repeated here.\n- It says the Engine does the NSFW filtering for keyed and keyless requests alike, separately from the gateway's block/dislike filter, and that it plays no part in the over-fetch.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:client/frontend/README.md": "<changes>\nI added the NSFW setting to `client/frontend/README.md`, widened the `feed-params.ts` bullet to cover it, and added `/api/v1/search/videos` to the list of gateway routes.\n\n- **Line 8:** `/api/v1/search/videos` is now in the list of gateway routes the frontend fetches.\n- **`feed-params.ts` bullet:** the module now covers the NSFW setting as well as the feed parameters. Feed parameters go through `buildSimilarUrl`, and the NSFW setting goes through `nsfwQuery`. Page code builds neither kind of query parameter itself.\n- **New NSFW setting bullet, after it.** Each point below was checked against the code:\n  - It is on by default and stored in `localStorage` under `nsfwFilter:v1` as `on`/`off`, apart from `feedParams:v1`. It does not follow a profile key to another browser.\n  - Only a stored `off` turns the filter off. A missing, corrupt or unreadable value means on. If a storage write fails, the choice still holds for the current page (the in-memory value in `setNsfwFilter`).\n  - Its only control is the \"Hide NSFW videos\" checkbox (`label.profile-nsfw`) in the home Profile modal. It appears in all three states and needs no key. The video and search pages have no control of their own.\n  - Changing it reloads the home feed. An older load that finishes later is discarded (the `current !== pager` guard in `loadVideos`).\n  - Home feed requests in every mode, up-next (the `?id=` view and the video page, through `buildSimilarUrl`) and search (`fetchSearchResults`) send `nsfw=1` only while the filter is off. The setting is read each time a request is built.\n  - For what `nsfw=1` includes, the bullet points to `engine/server/README.md` rather than restating the Engine's rules.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/OVERVIEW.md": "<changes>\nOVERVIEW.md now covers the NSFW filter: section 1, the up-next pool and its ANN fallback, the similarity and random caches, and the layer sources and pools.\n\nEach claim was checked against the code: `random_videos.fetch_random_rows_from_cache`, `handlers/similar._fetch_random_rows`, `similarity_candidates.get_upnext_candidates` / `get_similar_candidates`, and `builder.py`.\n\n- **Section 1, Random:** with the filter on, the draw makes up to `RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS` (4) cache windows. It drops rowids already seen and stops when the page is full or a window adds no unseen rowid. The DB draw, which is also filtered, runs only when that result is empty.\n- **Section 1, new \"NSFW filter\" bullet:** unless the request has `nsfw=1`, every mode and Up Next leave `videos.nsfw = 1` rows out while the pool or page is built, so pages stay full. For hot, recent and popular, `NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL` is inside the ordered query, so the paging walk steps through the filtered order. The parameter contract is pointed to in `engine/server/README.md` rather than repeated here.\n- **Excluded Videos:** \"Random is not filtered\" now reads \"Random does not apply `exclude`\", so it isn't read as being about NSFW.\n- **Section 2.3, up-next pool:**\n  - NSFW is added to the filter list, applied before the author cap and before the pool is counted.\n  - The ANN fallback stop rule is written as delivered. With `nsfw=1` a step that adds no row stops the ladder. With the filter on, the search keeps widening while the raw ANN hit count grows. Either way it stops at the target or at both caps.\n  - New bullet: the ANN compute and the cache write are unfiltered, so one shared cache entry serves both settings.\n- **Section 2.4, random cache:** points to `LAYER_PARAMS.md`, \"Random Cache Params\", for how the cache relates to the NSFW filter.\n- **Section 3, layers:** on the exploit layer, both the ANN and the cached like source drop flagged rows. The random layer points to the redraw described in section 1.\n- **Section 4, fetch limits:** every layer's source leaves flagged rows out. A like neighbourhood with many NSFW videos can leave the exploit pool short, so fallback fills its slots from other layers and the layer ratio shifts.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/LAYER_PARAMS.md": "<changes>\nLAYER_PARAMS.md now covers how the random cache and the up-next fallback work when the NSFW filter is on.\n\n- **Random Cache Params (Global):** added one paragraph after the build paragraph. The cache holds only rowids (the `random_rowids` table) and no NSFW flag, so the filter needs no rebuild or migration. The flag is read from `whitelist.db` when a draw's rowids are turned into rows. With the filter on, a draw takes up to `RANDOM_CACHE_NSFW_MAX_DRAWS` (4, `engine/server/data/random_videos.py`) cache windows. It takes `random_cache_lock` and then `db_lock` separately for each window. With the filter off, it takes one window. How the draw refills is left to `OVERVIEW.md` \u00a7 1, with a pointer there.\n- **Up-next Params \u2192 Pool and ANN Fallback:** the `SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_SEARCH_LIMIT`/`SIMILAR_VIDEO_MAX_NPROBE` bullet now says what happens with the filter on. The fallback keeps doubling past a step that adds only flagged hits, as long as the raw hit count grows, and it still stops at these caps.\n- I left the explore and random \"Source\" lines alone. Both already link to the Random Cache Params section, which now has the NSFW facts.\n- I checked each claim against the code:\n  - `random_cache.py`: the cache schema is `position` and `video_rowid` only.\n  - `fetch_random_rows_from_cache`: the draw loop and the locks it takes.\n  - The stop condition in `get_upnext_candidates`, `similarity_candidates.py:173`.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:CONTEXT.md": "<changes>\nI added an **NSFW filter** term to the `CONTEXT.md` glossary and named it in the **Block** entry as one more thing a block is distinct from.\n\n- **New entry, after Block.** It says:\n  - The NSFW filter is a per-browser setting, on by default, that makes the Engine leave `videos.nsfw = 1` rows out of every video listing: the home feed modes, up-next and search.\n  - It lives in the browser's `localStorage`, not on the profile, so it does not follow a profile key to another browser.\n  - A visitor opts out only by sending the exact value `nsfw=1`. Any other value, or none, means filtered.\n  - Videos whose flag is NULL are shown.\n  - It is distinct from a block, a dislike and operator moderation.\n  - A video page opened directly is never filtered.\n  - It cites ADR-0007, matching how the other entries cite their ADRs. That ADR is being written in its own turn on this checklist.\n- **Block entry.** The list of things a block is distinct from now includes the NSFW filter, \"which is a browser setting and needs no profile\".\n- **Checked against the code:** the exact-match rule (`_parse_include_nsfw` returns `value == \"1\"`), unset meaning filtered (`fetch_request_include_nsfw` defaults to False), the NULL rule (`NSFW_ALLOWED_SQL` in `engine/server/data/metadata.py`), and the `nsfwFilter:v1` key in `client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts`. The storage key and the list of routes are left to the READMEs that own them.\n- **Out of date, not fixed:** the docstring of `_parse_include_nsfw` in `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py` still says \"the gateway strips before forwarding\". Phase 3 made the gateway forward `nsfw` unstripped (`PROXY_UNSTRIPPED_QUERY_PARAMS`), so that sentence is now wrong. I left it alone because it is outside this file; it needs a one-line fix.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",

Per `docs/project/triage-labels.md`, the file moves to `issues/archive/`.\n- **Body:** the Problem, Requested behaviour, Proposed solution, Open questions and Related sections are left as they were, the same way the other archived issues (17, 37) keep them.\n- **Comments \u2192 Delivered:**\n  - It names the plan `docs/project/plans/22-36-nsfw-filter.md` and says \"Not yet committed\".\n  - It records each decision:\n    - Q1: no per-mode toggles; the Profile checkbox is the only control.\n    - Q2: what the filter covers.     "step_9_i2_update:engine/server/api/recommendations/docs/PIPELINE_DIAGRAM.md": "<changes>\nI added the NSFW filter to the pipeline diagram: a new request-context node after the request, and NSFW listed in the similarity candidate filters (node S) and the up-next pool filters (node U2).\n\n- **Intro paragraph:** one sentence saying every candidate source leaves NSFW-flagged rows out while its pool is built unless the request opts in. It points to `engine/server/README.md` for the `nsfw` parameter rather than repeating it.\n- **New node A0, between `Request /recommendations` and the likes-source node:** `nsfw` is parsed into the request context, only an exact `1` includes NSFW rows, and every candidate source applies the NSFW predicate.\n- **Node S:** adds \"NSFW unless nsfw=1\" after `error_threshold`.\n- **Node U2:** adds \"NSFW unless nsfw=1, before author caps\". This matches `_build_rows`, where a flagged entry finds no metadata and so takes no author slot.\n- **Node U4 (ANN fallback steps):** added a line not on the checklist item. With the filter on, the fallback keeps widening while the raw hit count grows. That is the stop rule at `similarity_candidates.py:173`.\n\nI checked each fact against the code: `_parse_include_nsfw`, `set_request_include_nsfw` in `_handle_similar`, the getter that returns False when unset, the builder's `fetch_include_nsfw` closures, `_build_rows`, and the ladder condition.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",
    "step_9_i2_update:docs/project/adr/": "<changes>\nAdded ADR-0007 (`docs/project/adr/0007-nsfw-filter-default-at-request-edge.md`), which records that the NSFW filter's default is set at the request edge and that the data layer defaults to unfiltered.\n\n- **Context:** names the callers that must stay unfiltered: `/api/video` and `/api/video/refresh`, the `/internal/*` resolution through `fetch_metadata_by_ids` and `fetch_metadata_by_uuids` in `internal_client_reads.py`, and the shared similarity cache (`ann.compute_similar_items`, then the write in `get_similar_candidates`).\n- **Decision:**\n  - The data-layer functions take `include_nsfw: bool = True`.\n  - The request edge sets the filtered default: `_handle_similar` and `_handle_search` parse `nsfw` with `_parse_include_nsfw`, which accepts only an exact `1`.\n  - `fetch_request_include_nsfw()` returns False when nothing was set, and `RecommendationBuilderDeps.fetch_include_nsfw` defaults to `lambda: False`.\n  - The similarity cache is filtered only in `_build_rows`, when rows are built.\n  - It also gives the reason a data layer that filters by default was rejected.\n- **Consequences:**\n  - Any new listing path must pass the flag, because the data layer shows NSFW rows by default.\n  - A new unfiltered read needs no change.\n  - The builder reads the flag on every call.\n  - The random cache stores no flag, so it needs no rebuild.\n\nI checked every claim against the code: `request_context.py:40-42`, `similar.py:1050` and `:1155`, `builder.py:64` and `:125`, `similarity_candidates.py:90-91`, and `internal_client_reads.py:157-159`.\n\nThe ADR links the issue at its archive path, `docs/project/issues/archive/36-nsfw-filter.md`, which is where that item's turn moves it.\n\nOne problem outside this file: the `_parse_include_nsfw` docstring in `engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py:1158` says \"the gateway strips before forwarding\". That is no longer true, because `PROXY_UNSTRIPPED_QUERY_PARAMS` forwards `nsfw` unstripped. I did not edit it.\n</changes>\n\n<not_on_checklist>\nnone\n</not_on_checklist>",

  "requirements": "### Purpose\n\nVideos flagged NSFW are hidden wherever the site lists videos, unless the visitor opts in. Today every video has a nullable `nsfw` INTEGER column in `whitelist.db` (`videos.nsfw`). The crawler fills it, and `/api/video` refreshes it from the source instance (issue 10). The Engine selects the column and passes it through (`engine/server/data/random_videos.py`, `metadata.py`, `search.py`), but nothing filters on it, and `client/frontend` has no NSFW control. After this build a visitor who does nothing never sees an NSFW-flagged video in any list.\n\n### The setting\n\n- A single NSFW setting. Its only control is in the Profile modal (`#profile-section`, rendered by `renderProfileSection` in `client/frontend/src/pages/videos/index.ts`).\n- The control appears in every state the modal renders: a keyless visitor, a visitor holding a key, and the just-issued-key view. It needs no profile key.\n- Default: filter on (NSFW hidden). Turning it off shows NSFW videos.\n- The setting applies everywhere listed under \"Coverage\". There is no other control.\n- Changing the setting on the home page reloads the current feed, so the change shows immediately.\n\n### No per-mode toggles\n\nThe request's toggle buttons on the Recommendations and Random feed modes are dropped at the operator's decision. The feed-mode switcher (`[data-feed-mode]` buttons) is unchanged.\n\n### Storage\n\n- The setting is stored in the browser's `localStorage` only, next to `feedParams:v1` (`client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts`). It persists across reloads.\n- It is not stored server-side and does not follow a profile key to another browser.\n- Missing, unreadable (quota or private mode) or corrupt storage means filter on. A storage write failure must not break the page; the choice still holds for the current page.\n\n### Coverage\n\nThe filter applies to every video list the site requests from the Engine:\n- All five home feed modes: Recommendations, Hot, Recent, Random and Popular (`/recommendations` with `mode=`).\n- The up-next feed: `/videos/similar` and `/recommendations` with a seed `id`, as requested by the video page (`client/frontend/src/pages/video-page/index.ts`) and by the home page with `?id=`.\n- Search (`/api/v1/search/videos`, `client/frontend/src/pages/search/index.ts`).\n\nThe channels page (`client/frontend/src/pages/channels`) lists channels only and fetches no video rows, so it is unaffected.\n\n### Filtering happens in the Engine\n\n- The Engine leaves NSFW rows out while it builds each pool or page, so a page is still filled to its requested size. This covers the home like-layer and mixer layer pools (layer slots filled by ratio), the up-next pool (about 17 rows deep, then the weighted draw), the ordered Hot/Recent/Popular pages (LIMIT/OFFSET paging must not skip or repeat rows under the filter), the random draw, and search results.\n- The browser never drops rows from a page after it arrives, and the gateway (`client/backend/server.py`) does not filter NSFW rows out of the payload either.\n- With the filter off, results are identical to today's.\n\n### Request parameter\n\n- One query parameter, `nsfw`. `nsfw=1` means include NSFW rows. A missing parameter, an empty value, or any other value means filtered. A request that omits it never receives an NSFW-flagged row.\n- The frontend sends `nsfw=1` only when the visitor has turned the filter off, on every feed, up-next and search request.\n- The gateway allowlist `PROXY_ALLOWED_QUERY_PARAMS` in `client/backend/server.py` gains `nsfw` for `/recommendations`, `/videos/similar` and `/api/v1/search/videos`, and the gateway forwards it to the Engine.\n\n### Unknown flags\n\n`nsfw` NULL counts as not NSFW: with the filter on, only rows with `nsfw = 1` are removed (`v.nsfw IS NULL OR v.nsfw = 0` passes). The operator chose this without a measurement, and no `whitelist.db` is in the tree to measure against.\n\n### Random feed page size\n\n`random-cache.db` is prebuilt and holds rowids (`data/random_cache.fetch_random_rowids`, then `data/metadata.fetch_metadata`). With the filter on, the Random feed must still return a full page. The design chooses and justifies one of two approaches: read each drawn video's flag at draw time and draw again or overdraw to refill, or store the flag in the cache. If the cache schema changes, the rebuild and upgrade path must be stated.\n\n### Out of scope\n\n- A warning or overlay on a video page opened directly (for example from a link) for an NSFW video. The video page plays whatever it is linked to.\n- Server-side storage of the setting on the profile key (`user_db`).\n- Toggle buttons on individual feed modes.\n\n### Baseline suite state\n\nThe pre-build suite exited 0 (baseline variant: false). The run selected `test_search_fusion.py` (10 passed); the other 29 test groups were unchanged. The build must leave the suite green.",

  "initial_solution": "### Approach\n\nOne request flag, `include_nsfw`, is parsed once at the Engine's edge. It travels explicitly wherever the call chain is short. Where the call chain runs through the recommendation strategy's generator protocol, it goes through the request context that already carries excluded keys, likes and dislike centroids. Filtering is a SQL predicate, `(v.nsfw IS NULL OR v.nsfw = 0)`, added to the queries that build each pool, so LIMITs count only rows that are allowed. Nothing drops rows after a page is assembled.\n\n**Engine edge (`engine/server/api/handlers/similar.py`).** A parser treats only the exact value `1` as include. It deliberately does not use `_parse_bool`, which also accepts `true`, `yes` and `on`; the requirement says any other value means filtered. `_handle_similar` covers the POST `/recommendations` and `/videos/similar` routes and the GET `/videos/{id}/similar` alias. It parses `nsfw` from the query and stores it in the request context through a new setter and getter pair in `request_context.py`. The getter returns \"filtered\" when the value is unset, and `clear_request_context` clears it. `_handle_search` parses it the same way and passes it to `search_videos`. A request without the parameter is filtered on every route.\n\n**Data layer: an explicit keyword whose default keeps today's behaviour.** `fetch_metadata`, `fetch_metadata_by_ids` / `_select_metadata`, `fetch_random_rows`, `fetch_recent_videos`, `fetch_popular_videos`, `fetch_ordered_page`, `fetch_random_rows_from_cache`, `lexical_candidates`, `vector_candidates` and `search_videos` each gain `include_nsfw: bool = True`. When it is False they add the predicate next to the existing `error_threshold` clause, which already uses the same WHERE/AND pattern. The default stays include because these helpers also serve non-listing callers that must not change: `/api/video` (the video page plays whatever it is linked to), `/internal/videos/*` (resolving likes and blocks), and the ANN compute that writes the similarity cache. \"Filtered by default\" is enforced at the request edge, not in the data layer.\n\n**How each coverage item is met:**\n- **Hot, Recent and Popular (ordered pages).** `_handle_ordered_feed` passes the flag to `fetch_ordered_page`, so the predicate sits inside the ordered query. OFFSET then counts over the filtered total order, and each chunk continues exactly where the last ended. Rows are neither skipped nor repeated, and NSFW rows no longer use up the `ORDERED_FEED_MAX_CHUNKS` budget.\n- **Random feed, the home fallback and the random seed path.** `_fetch_random_rows` passes the flag to both the cache draw and the `ORDER BY RANDOM()` fallback. The cache refill is described under \"Random feed page size\" below.\n- **Recommendations (mixer).** `RecommendationBuilderDeps` gains `fetch_include_nsfw`. It defaults to a callable that returns False, so the keyword construction in `tests/active/test_video.py` still builds, and `server.py` wires in the request-context getter. The builder's existing `*_filtered` closures pass the flag into the random, cache, recent and popular fetches, so those layers are filled at the SQL level. The builder also wraps `get_similar_candidates` so the like-layer sources run with a policy carrying the flag. `SimilarityCandidatesPolicy` gains `include_nsfw`, and the sources stay unchanged.\n- **Like layer and up-next pools.** `_build_rows` in `data/similarity_candidates.py` passes the flag to `fetch_metadata_by_ids`. NSFW entries find no metadata and are skipped before the author cap and before the count toward `limit`. `UpnextPoolPolicy` gains `include_nsfw`, set by `_handle_seed_with_embedding`. `_upnext_rows` counts the filtered pool, so the existing floored ANN fallback widens nprobe and search_limit until `target_min_pool` (about 17) is reached, and only then does the weighted draw run. The refill this needs is the mechanism that already exists. `_handle_vector_search` passes the flag too.\n- **Search.** `lexical_candidates` puts the predicate in the FTS query, so its `candidate_pool` LIMIT counts only allowed rows. `vector_candidates` passes the flag to `fetch_metadata`. The fused list, its `total` and page slicing are all computed after filtering, so pages stay consistent.\n- **Filter off.** Every change is an added clause or an extra draw that runs only when the flag is False. With `nsfw=1` the SQL, the draws and the pools are byte-for-byte today's.\n\n**Random feed page size: read the flag at draw time and redraw.** When the filter is on, `fetch_random_rows_from_cache` draws its usual contiguous window, resolves it with `fetch_metadata(include_nsfw=False)`, and draws further random windows while the page is short. It skips rowids already seen and appends in draw order until the page reaches `limit`. The number of draws is capped by a named constant (4, matching `ORDERED_FEED_MAX_CHUNKS`). With the filter off it makes exactly one draw, as today. That matters: always refilling would also start refilling pages that `error_threshold` drops short, which would change filter-off results. The cache schema does not change, so no rebuild or upgrade is needed.\n\n**Gateway (`client/backend/server.py`).** `nsfw` is added to the `PROXY_ALLOWED_QUERY_PARAMS` sets for `/recommendations`, `/videos/similar` and `/api/v1/search/videos`. The existing sanitiser already forwards allowed parameters and drops empty values; an empty value correctly becomes \"missing\" and so \"filtered\". The gateway's row filter (blocks and dislikes) is not touched, and it does not look at `nsfw`.\n\n**Frontend.**\n- **Storage (`client/frontend/src/data/feed-params.ts`).** The setting lives here under its own key, `nsfwFilter:v1`. The module gains read, set and query-entry helpers. Only a stored value that explicitly means \"off\" turns the filter off; a missing, unreadable or corrupt value reads as on. A module-level in-memory value holds the choice when `setItem` throws, so it still applies on the current page. This is the same try/ignore pattern `persistFeedParams` uses.\n- **Requests.** `buildSimilarUrl` in `data/videos.ts` appends `nsfw=1` when the filter is off. The keyless search cache is keyed by URL, so on and off results never share a cache entry.\n- **Control (`renderProfileSection` in `pages/videos/index.ts`).** A small helper builds a \"Hide NSFW videos\" checkbox, checked by default. The cache is prebuilt and refreshed only on an interval, while `nsfw` in `whitelist.db` changes whenever the crawler or an `/api/video` refresh updates it. A cached flag would go stale and let a newly flagged video through until the next rebuild, breaking \"never sees\". The draw already joins `videos` in `fetch_metadata`, so reading the live flag costs nothing. Storing the flag would also need a schema change, a change to the `precompute-random-rowids` job, a forced rebuild of every deployed cache, and a reader for old caches.\n- **A data-layer default of \"filtered\".** Rejected. It would hide NSFW videos from `/api/video`, from internal like and block resolution, and from the ANN compute that writes the shared similarity cache. That breaks \"the video page plays whatever it is linked to\" and poisons the cache for visitors who opt in.\n- **Filtering inside the ANN compute, so cached similarity lists are NSFW-free.** Rejected. The cache is shared across requests, and with the filter off results must be identical to today's. Filtering has to happen after the cache is read (`_build_rows`), never before it is written.\n- **Passing the flag as an argument through `generate_recommendations` and every generator's `get_candidates`.** Rejected. It changes the Protocol and five generators plus two sources. The request context exists for exactly this kind of per-request value, and the builder already reads excluded keys from it through a dep.\n- **Folding the setting into the `feedParams:v1` object.** Rejected. `resolveFeedParams` skips storage when `?mode=` is present and returns only `{mode}`, and `chooseFeedMode` overwrites the object. The NSFW setting also applies to search and the video page, which never read feed params. A separate key keeps the two lifecycles apart.\n- **Reusing `_parse_bool` for the parameter.** Rejected. It accepts `true`, `yes` and `on`, and the requirement says only `1` includes NSFW.\n\n### Gotchas and risks\n\n- **The include default is a footgun.** A future listing call site that forgets to pass the flag would leak NSFW rows. Tests should pin each listing path (the five modes, `?id=` up-next, the video page's up-next, search, the random fallback and the vector path) against a fixture with `nsfw=1`, `0` and NULL rows, requested without the parameter.\n- **The existing suite relies on NULL flags.** `test_similar.py` compares the HTTP ordered feed, sent without `nsfw`, against `fetch_ordered_page` called at its default. A visitor whose likes sit in mostly NSFW neighbourhoods gets a smaller like layer, and the mixer's existing backfill fills those slots from other layers. The page is still full, but the layer ratio shifts for that visitor.
